book.title: The Upanishads
book.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)
book.license: Public domain translations (Müller, 1879 and 1884); proofread transcription from Wikisource.
book.notes: Seven of the principal Upanishads as Müller translated and numbered them: Chandogya, Kena (Talavakâra), Aitareya, Katha, Mundaka, Prasna and Taittiriya. The Aitareya is the Upanishad proper from Müller’s Aitareya-âranyaka (second âranyaka, adhyâyas 4–6), lifted out of the surrounding ritual text. The Sanskrit text is not part of this edition. Brihadâranyaka, Svetâsvatara and Maitrâyana are not bundled; see the registry for the reason.

verses.translation: Let a man meditate on the syllable Om, called the udgîtha; for the udgîtha (a portion of the Sâma-veda) is sung, beginning with Om.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The full account, however, of Om is this:—
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The essence of all beings is the earth, the essence of the earth is water, the essence of water the plants, the essence of plants man, the essence of man speech, the essence of speech the Rig-veda, the essence of the Rig-veda the Sâma-veda, the essence of the Sâma-veda the udgîtha (which is Om).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: That udgîtha (Om) is the best of all essences, the highest, deserving the highest place, the eighth.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: What then is the Rik? What is the Sâman? What is the udgîtha? This is the question.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The Rik indeed is speech, Sâman is breath, the udgîtha is the syllable Om. Now speech and breath, or Rik and Sâman, form one couple.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And that couple is joined together in the syllable Om. When two people come together, they fulfil each other's desire.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Thus he who knowing this, meditates on the syllable (Om), the udgîtha, becomes indeed a fulfiller of desires.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: That syllable is a syllable of permission, for whenever we permit anything, we say Om, yes. Now permission is gratification. He who knowing this meditates on the syllable (Om), the udgîtha, becomes indeed a gratifier of desires.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: By that syllable does the threefold knowledge (the sacrifice, more particularly the Soma-sacrifice, as founded on the three Vedas) proceed. When the Adhvaryu priest gives an order, he says Om. When the Hotri priest recites, he says Om. When the Udgâtri priest sings, he says Om, —all for the glory of that syllable. The threefold knowledge (the sacrifice) proceeds by the greatness of that syllable (the vital breaths), and by its essence (the oblations).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Now therefore it would seem to follow, that both he who knows this (the true meaning of the syllable Om), and he who does not, perform the same sacrifice. But this is not so, for knowledge and ignorance are different. The sacrifice which a man performs with knowledge, faith, and the Upanishad is more powerful. This is the full account of the syllable Om.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Whent he Devas and Asuras struggled together, both of the race of Pragâpati, the Devas took the udgîtha (Om), thinking they would vanquish the Asuras with it.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They meditated on the udgîtha (Om) as the breath (scent) in the nose, but the Asuras pierced it (the breath) with evil. Therefore we smell by the breath in the nose both what is good-smelling and what is bad-smelling. For the breath was pierced by evil.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then they meditated on the udgîtha (Om) as speech, but the Asuras pierced it with evil. Therefore we speak both truth and falsehood. For speech is pierced by evil.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then they meditated on the udgîtha (Om) as the eye, but the Asuras pierced it with evil. Therefore we see both what is sightly and unsightly. For the eye is pierced by evil.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then they meditated on the udgîtha (Om) as the ear, but the Asuras pierced it with evil. Therefore we hear both what should be heard and what should not be heard. For the ear is pierced by evil.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then they meditated on the udgîtha (Om) as the mind, but the Asuras pierced it with evil. Therefore we conceive both what should be conceived and what should not be conceived. For the mind is pierced by evil.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then comes this breath (of life) in the mouth. They meditated on the udgîtha (Om) as that breath. When the Asuras came to it, they were scattered, as (a ball of earth) would be scattered when hitting a solid stone.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Thus, as a ball of earth is scattered when hitting on a solid stone, will he be scattered who wishes evil to one who knows this, or who persecutes him; for he is a solid stone.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: By it (the breath in the mouth) he distinguishes neither what is good nor what is bad-smelling, for that breath is free from evil. What we eat and drink with it supports the other vital breaths (i. e. the senses, such as smell, &c.) When at the time of death he does not find that breath (in the mouth, through which he eats and drinks and lives), then he departs. He opens the mouth at the time of death (as if wishing to eat).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Angiras meditated on the udgîtha (Om) as that breath, and people hold it to be Angiras, i. e. the essence of the members (angânâm rasah);
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Therefore Brihaspati meditated on udgîtha (Om) as that breath, and people hold it to be Brihaspati, for speech is brihatî, and he (that breath) is the lord (pati) of speech;
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Therefore Ayâsya meditated on the udgîtha (Om) as that breath, and people hold it to be Ayâsya, because it comes (ayati) from the mouth (âsya);
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Therefore Vaka Dâlbhya knew it. He was the Udgâtri (singer) of the Naimishîya-sacrificers, and by singing he obtained for them their wishes.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who knows this, and meditates on the syllable Om (the imperishable udgîtha) as the breath of life in the mouth, he obtains all wishes by singing. So much for the udgîtha (Om) as meditated on with reference to the body.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Now follows the meditation on the udgîtha with reference to the gods. Let a man meditate on the udgîtha (Om) as he who sends warmth (the sun in the sky). When the sun rises it sings as Udgâtri for the sake of all creatures. When it rises it destroys the fear of darkness. He who knows this, is able to destroy the fear of darkness (ignorance).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: This (the breath in the mouth) and that (the sun) are the same. This is hot and that is hot. This they call svara (sound), and that they call pratyâsvara (reflected sound). Therefore let a man meditate on the udgîtha (Om) as this and that (as breath and as sun).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then let a man meditate on the udgîtha (Om) as vyâna indeed. If we breathe up, that is prâna, the up-breathing. If we breathe down, that is apâna, the down-breathing. The combination of prâna and apâna is vyâna, back-breathing or holding in of the breath. This vyâna is speech. Therefore when we utter speech, we neither breathe up nor down.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Rik is Sâman, and therefore when a man utters a Sâman verse he neither breathes up nor down.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Sâman is udgîtha, and therefore when a man sings (the udgîtha, Om) he neither breathes up nor down.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And other works also which require strength, such as the production of fire by rubbing, running a race, stringing a strong bow, are performed without breathing up or down. Therefore let a man meditate on the udgîtha (Om) as vyâna.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Let a man meditate on the syllables of the udgîtha, i. e. of the word udgîtha. Ut is breath (prâna), for by means of breath a man rises (uttishthati). Gî is speech, for speeches are called girah. Tha is food, for by means of food all subsists (sthita).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Ut is heaven, gî the sky, tha the earth. Ut is the sun, gî the air, tha the fire. Ut is the Sâma-veda, gî the Yagur-veda, tha the Rig-veda. Speech yields the milk, which is the milk of speech itself, to him who thus knowing meditates on those syllables of the name of udgîtha, he becomes rich in food and able to eat food.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Next follows the fulfilment of prayers. Let a man thus meditate on the Upasaranas, i. e. the objects which have to be approached by meditation: Let him (the Udgâtri) quickly reflect on the Sâman with which he is going to praise;
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Let him quickly reflect on the Rik in which that Sâman occurs; on the Rishi (poet) by whom it was seen or composed; on the Devatâ (object) which he is going to praise;
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: On the metre in which he is going to praise; on the tune with which he is going to sing for himself;
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: On the quarter of the world which he is going to praise. Lastly, having approached himself (his name, family, &c.) by meditation, let him sing the hymn of praise, reflecting on his desire, and avoiding all mistakes in pronunciation, &c. Quickly will the desire be then fulfilled to him, for the sake of which he may have offered his hymn of praise, yea, for which he may have offered his hymn of praise.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Let a man meditate on the syllable Om, for the udgîtha is sung beginning with Om. And this is the full account of the syllable Om:—
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The Devas, being afraid of death, entered upon (the performance of the sacrifice prescribed in) the threefold knowledge (the three Vedas). They covered themselves with the metrical hymns. Because they covered (khad) themselves with the hymns, therefore the hymns are called khandas.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then, as a fisherman might observe a fish in the water, Death observed the Devas in the Rik, Yagus, and Sâman-(sacrifices). And the Devas seeing this, rose from the Rik, Yagus, and Sâman-sacrifices, and entered the Svara, i.e. the Om (they meditated on the Om).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: When a man has mastered the Rig-veda, he says quite loud Om; the same, when he has mastered the Sâman and the Yagus. This Svara is the imperishable (syllable), the immortal, free from fear. Because the Devas entered it, therefore they became immortal, and free from fear.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who knowing this loudly pronounces (pranauti) that syllable, enters the same (imperishable) syllable, the Svara, the immortal, free from fear, and having entered it, becomes immortal, as the Devas are immortal.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The udgîtha is the pranava, the pranava is the udgîtha. And as the udgîtha is the sun, so is the pranava, for he (the sun) goes sounding Om.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Him I sang praises to, therefore art thou my only one,' thus said Kaushîtaki to his son. 'Do thou revolve his rays, then thou wilt have many sons.' So much in reference to the Devas.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Now with reference to the body. Let a man meditate on the udgîtha as the breath (in the mouth), for he goes sounding Om.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Him I sang praises to, therefore art thou my only son,' thus said Kaushîtaki to his son. 'Do thou therefore sing praises to the breath as manifold, if thou wishest to have many sons.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who knows that the udgîtha is the pranava, and the pranava the udgîtha, rectifies from the seat of the Hotri priest any mistake committed by the Udgâtri priest in performing the udgîtha, yea, in performing the udgîtha.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The Rik (veda) is this earth, the Sâman (veda) is fire. This Sâman (fire) rests on that Rik (earth). Therefore the Sâman is sung as resting on the Rik. Sâ is this earth, ama is fire, and that makes Sâma.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The Rik is the sky, the Sâman air. This Sâman (air) rests on that Rik (sky). Therefore the Sâman is sung as resting on the Rik. Sâ is the sky, ama the air, and that makes Sâma.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Rik is heaven, Sâman the sun. This Sâman (sun) rests on that Rik (heaven). Therefore the Sâman is sung as resting on the Rik. Sâ is heaven, ama the sun, and that makes Sâma.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Rik is the stars, Sâman the moon. This Sâman (moon) rests on that Rik (stars). Therefore the Sâman is sung as resting on the Rik. Sâ is the stars, ama the moon, and that makes Sâma.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Rik is the white light of the sun, Sâman the blue exceeding darkness (in the sun). This Sâman (darkness) rests on that Rik (brightness). Therefore the Sâman is sung as resting on the Rik.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Sâ is the white light of the sun, ama the blue exceeding darkness, and that makes Sâma.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Now that golden person, who is seen within the sun, with golden beard and golden hair, golden altogether to the very tips of his nails,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Whose eyes are like blue lotus's, his name is ut, for he has risen (udita) above all evil. He also who knows this, rises above all evil.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Rik and Sâman are his joints, and therefore he is udgîtha. And therefore he who praises him (the ut) is called the Ud-gâtri (the out-singer). He (the golden person, called ut) is lord of the worlds beyond that (sun), and of all the wishes of the Devas (inhabiting those worlds). So much with reference to the Devas.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Now with reference to the body. Rik is speech, Sâman breath. This Sâman (breath) rests on that Rik (speech). Therefore the Sâman is sung as resting on the Rik. Sâ is speech, ama is breath, and that makes Sâma.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Rik is the eye, Sâman the self. This Sâman (shadow) rests on that Rik (eye). Therefore the Sâman is sung as resting on the Rik. Sâ is the eye, ama the self, and that makes Sâma.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Rik is the ear, Sâman the mind. This Sâman (mind) rests on that Rik (ear). Therefore the Sâman is sung as resting on the Rik. Sâ is the ear, ama the mind, and that makes Sâma.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Rik is the white light of the eye, Sâman the blue exceeding darkness. This Sâman (darkness) rests on the Rik (brightness). Therefore the Sâman is sung as resting on the Rik. Sâ is the white light of the eye, ama the blue exceeding darkness, and that makes Sâma.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Now the person who is seen in the eye, he is Rik, he is Sâman, Uktha, Yagus, Brahman. The form of that person (in the eye) is the same as the form of the other person (in the sun), the joints of the one (Rik and Sâman) are the joints of the other, the name of the one (ut) is the name of the other.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He is lord of the worlds beneath that (the self in the eye), and of all the wishes of men. Therefore all who sing to the vînâ (lyre), sing him, and from him also they obtain wealth.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who knowing this sings a Sâman, sings to both (the adhidaivata and adhyâtma self, the person in the sun and the person in the eye, as one and the same person). He obtains through the one, yea, he obtains the worlds beyond that, and the wishes of the Devas;
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And he obtains through the other the worlds beneath that, and the wishes of men.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Therefore an Udgâtri priest who knows this, may say (to the sacrificer for whom he officiates);
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: "What wish shall I obtain for you by my songs?" For he who knowing this sings a Sâman is able to obtain wishes through his song, yea, through his song.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: There were once three men, well-versed in udgîtha, Silaka Sâlâvatya, Kaikitâyana Dâlbhya, and Pravâhana Gaivali. They said: 'We are well-versed in udgîtha. Let us have a discussion on udgîtha.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They all agreed and sat down. Then Pravâhana Gaivali said: 'Sirs, do you both speak first, for I wish to hear what two Brâhmanas have to say.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then Silaka Sâlâvatya said to Kaikitâyana Dâlbhya: 'Let me ask you.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Ask,' he replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'What is the origin of the Sâman?' 'Tone (svara),' he replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'What is the origin of tone?' 'Breath,' he replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'What is the origin of breath?' 'Food,' he replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'What is the origin of food?' 'Water,' he replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'What is the origin of water?' 'That world (heaven),' he replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And what is the origin of that world?'—
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He replied: 'Let no man carry the Sâman beyond the world of svarga (heaven). We place (recognise) the Sâman in the world of svarga, for the Sâman is extolled as svarga (heaven).'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then said Silaka Sâlâvatya to Kaikitâyana Dâlbhya: 'O Dâlbhya, thy Sâman is not firmly established. And if any one were to say, Your head shall fall off (if you be wrong), surely your head would now fall.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Well then, let me know this from you, Sir,' said Dâlbhya.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Know it,' replied Silaka Sâlâvatya.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'What is the origin of that world (heaven)?' 'This world,' he replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And what is the origin of this world?'—
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He replied: 'Let no man carry the Sâman beyond this world as its rest. We place the Sâman
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: in this world as its rest, for the Sâman is extolled as rest.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then said Pravâhana Gaivali to Silaka Sâlâvatya: 'Your Sâman (the earth), O Sâlâvatya, has an end. And if any one were to say, Your head shall fall off (if you be wrong), surely your head would now fall.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Well then, let me know this from you, Sir,' said Sâlâvatya.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Know it,' replied Gaivali.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'What is the origin of this world?' 'Ether,' he replied. For all these beings take their rise from the ether, and return into the ether. Ether is older than these, ether is their rest.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He is indeed the udîttha (Om=Brahman), greater than great (parovarîyas), he is without end. He who knowing this meditates on the udgîtha, the greater than great, obtains what is greater than great, he conquers the worlds which are greater than great.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Atidhanvan Saunaka, having taught this udgîtha to Udara-sândilya, said: 'As long as they will know in your family this udgîtha, their life in this world will be greater than great.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And thus also will be their state in the other world.' He who thus knows the udgîtha, and meditates on it thus, his life in this world will be greater than great, and also his state in the other world, yea, in the other world.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: When the Kurus had been destroyed by (hail) stones, Ushasti Kâkrâyana lived as a beggar with his virgin wife at Ibhyagrâma.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Seeing a chief eating beans, he begged of him. The chief said: 'I have no more, except those which are put away for me here.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Ushasti said: 'Give me to eat of them.' He gave him the beans, and said: 'There is something to drink also.' Then said Ushasti: 'If I drank of it, I should have drunk what was left by another, and is therefore unclean.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The chief said: 'Were not those beans also left over and therefore unclean?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'No,' he replied; 'for I should not have lived, if I had not eaten them, but the drinking of water would be mere pleasure.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Having eaten himself, Ushasti gave the remaining beans to his wife. But she, having eaten before, took them and put them away.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Rising the next morning, Ushasti said to her: 'Alas, if we could only get some food, we might gain a little wealth. The king here is going to offer a sacrifice, he should choose me for all the priestly offices.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: His wife said to him: 'Look, here are those beans of yours.' Having eaten them, he went to the sacrifice which was being performed.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He went and sat down on the orchestra near the Udgâtris, who were going to sing their hymns of praise. And he said to the Prastotri (the leader):
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Prastotri, if you, without knowing the deity which belongs to the prastâva (the hymns &c. of the Prastotri), are going to sing it, your head will fall off.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: In the same manner he addressed the Udgâtri; 'Udgâtri, if you, without knowing the deity which belongs to the udgtîha (the hymns of the Udgâtri), are going to sing it, your head will fall off.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: In the same manner he addressed the Pratihartri; 'Pratihartri, if you, without knowing the deity which belongs to the pratihâra (the hymns of the Pratihartri), are going to sing it, your head will fall off.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They stopped, and sat down in silence.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then the sacrificer said to him: 'I should like to know who you are, Sir.' He replied: 'I am Ushasti Kâkrâyana.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said: 'I looked for you, Sir, for all these sacrificial offices, but not finding you, I chose others.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'But now, Sir, take all the sacrificial offices.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Ushasti said: "Very well; but let those, with my permission, perform the hymns of praise. Only as much wealth as you give to them, so much give to me also.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The sacrificer assented.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then the Prastotri approached him, saying: 'Sir, you said to me, "Prastotri, if you, without knowing the deity which belongs to the prastâva, are going to sing it, your head will fall off,"—which then is that deity?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said: 'Breath (prâna). For all these beings merge into breath alone, and from breath they arise. This is the deity belonging to the prastâva. If, without knowing that deity, you had sung forth your hymns, your head would have fallen off, after you had been warned by me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then the Udgâtri approached him, saying: 'Sir, you said to me, "Udgâtri, if you, without knowing the deity which belongs to the udgîtha, are going to sing it, your head will fall off,"—which then is that deity?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said: 'The sun (âditya). For all these beings praise the sun when it stands on high. This is the deity belonging to the udgîtha. If without knowing that deity, you had sung out your hymns, your head would have fallen off, after you had been warned by me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then the Pratihartri approached him, saying: 'Sir, you said to me, "Pratihartri, if you, without knowing the deity belonging to the pratihâra, are going to sing it, your head will fall off,"—which then is that deity?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said: 'Food (anna). For all these beings live when they partake of food. This is the deity belonging to the pratihâra. If, without knowing that deity, you had sung your hymns, your head would have fallen off, after you had been warned by me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Now follows the udgîtha of the dogs. Vaka Dâlbhya, or, as he was also called, Glâva Maitreya, went out to repeat the Veda (in a quiet place).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: A white (dog) appeared before him, and other dogs gathering round him, said to him: 'Sir, sing and get us food, we are hungry.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The white dog said to them: 'Come to me to-morrow morning.' Vaka Dâlbhya, or, as he was also called, Glâva Maitreya, watched.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The dogs came on, holding together, each dog keeping the tail of the preceding dog in his mouth, as the priests do when they are going to sing praises with the Vahishpavamâna hymn. After they had settled down, they began to say Hin.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Om, let us eat! Om, let us drink! Om, may the divine Varuna, Pragâpati, Savitri bring us food! Lord of food, bring hither food, bring it, Om!'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The syllable Hâu is this world (the earth), the syllable Hâi the air, the syllable Atha the moon, the syllable Iha the self, the syllable Î is Agni, fire.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The syllable Û is the sun, the syllable E is the Nihava or invocation, the syllable Auhoi is the Visve Devas, the syllable Hin is Pragâpati, Svara (tone) is breath (prâna), the syllable Yâ is food, the syllable Vâg is Virâg.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The thirteenth stobha syllable, viz. the indistinct syllable Huṅ, is the Undefinable (the Highest Brahman).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Speech yields the milk, which is the milk of speech itself to him who knows this Upanishad (secret doctrine) of the Sâmans in this wise. He becomes rich in food, and able to eat food,—yea, able to eat food.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Meditation on the whole of the Sâman is good, and people, when anything is good, say it is Sâman; when it is not good, it is not Sâman.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Thus they also say, he approached him with Sâman, i.e. becomingly; and he approached him without Sâman, i. e. unbecomingly.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And they also say, truly this is Sâman for us, i.e. it is good for us, when it is good; and truly that is not Sâman for us, i. e. it is not good for us, when it is not good.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: If any one knowing this meditates on the Sâman as good, depend upon it all good qualities will approach quickly, aye, they will become his own.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Let a man meditate on the fivefold Sâman as the five worlds. The hinkâra is the earth, the prastâva the fire, the udgîtha the sky, the pratihâra the sun, the nidhana heaven; so in an ascending line.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: In a descending line, the hinkâra is heaven, the prastâva the sun, the udgîtha the sky, the pratihâra the fire, the nidhana the earth.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The worlds in an ascending and in a descending line belong to him who knowing this meditates on the fivefold Sâman as the worlds.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Let a man meditate on the fivefold Sâman as rain. The hinkâra is wind (that brings the rain); the prastâva is, 'the cloud is come'; the udgîtha is, 'it rains;' the pratihâra, 'it flashes, it thunders;'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The nidhana is, 'it stops.' There is rain for him, and he brings rain for others who thus knowing meditates on the fivefold Sâman as rain.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Let a man meditate on the fivefold Sâman in all waters. When the clouds gather, that is the hinkâra; when it rains, that is the prastâva; that which flows in the east, that is the udgîtha; that which flows in the west, that is the pratihâra; the sea is the nidhana.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He does not die in water, nay, he is rich in water who knowing this meditates on the fivefold Sâman as all waters.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Let a man meditate on the fivefold Sâman as the seasons. The hinkâra is spring, the prastâva summer (harvest of yava, &c), the udgîtha the rainy season, the pratihâra autumn, the nidhana winter.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The seasons belong to him, nay, he is always in season (successful) who knowing this meditates on the fivefold Sâman as the seasons.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Let a man meditate on the fivefold Sâman in animals. The hinkâra is goats, the prastâva sheep, the udgîtha cows, the pratihâra horses, the nidhana man.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Animals belong to him, nay, he is rich in animals who knowing this meditates on the fivefold Sâman as animals.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Let a man meditate on the fivefold Sâman, which is greater than great, as the prânas (senses). The hinkâra is smell (nose), the prastâva speech (tongue), the udgîtha sight (eye), the pratihâra hearing (ear), the nidhana mind. These are one greater than the other.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: What is greater than great belongs to him, nay, he conquers the worlds which are greater than great, who knowing this meditates on the fivefold Sâman, which is greater than great, as the prânas (senses).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Next for the sevenfold Sâman. Let a man meditate on the sevenfold Sâman in speech. Whenever there is in speech the syllable hun that is hinkâra, pra is the prastâva, â is the âdi, the first, i. e. Om,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Ud is the udgîtha, pra the pratihâra, upa the upadrava, ni the nidhana.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Speech yields the milk, which is the milk of speech itself, to him who knowing this meditates on the sevenfold Sâman in speech. He becomes rich in food, and able to eat food.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Let a man meditate on the sevenfold Sâman as the sun. The sun is Sâman, because he is always the same (sama); he is Sâman because he is the same, everybody thinking he looks towards me, he looks towards me.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Let him know that all beings are dependent on him (the sun). What he is before his rising, that is the hinkâra. On it animals are dependent. Therefore animals say hin (before sunrise), for they share the hinkâra of that Sâman (the sun).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: What he is at the time of the sangava, that is the âdi, the first, the Om. On it birds are dependent. Therefore birds fly about in the sky without support, holding themselves, for they share the âdi (the Om) of that Sâman.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: What he is just at noon, that is the udgîtha. On it the Devas are dependent (because they are brilliant). Therefore they are the best of all the descendants of Pragâpati, for they share the udgîtha of that Sâman.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: What he is after midday and before afternoon, that is the pratihâra. On it all germs are dependent. Therefore these, having been conceived (pratihrita), do not fall, for they share the pratihâra of that Sâman.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: What he is after the afternoon and before sunset, that is the upadrava. On it the animals of the forest are dependent. Therefore, when they see a man, they run (upadravanti) to the forest as a safe hiding-place, for they share the upadrava of that Sâman.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: What he is when he first sets, that is the nidhana. On it the fathers are dependent Therefore they put them down (nidadhati), for they share the nidhana of that Sâman. Thus a man meditates on the sevenfold Sâman as the sun.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Next let a man meditate on the sevenfold Sâman which is uniform in itself and leads beyond death. The word hinkâra has three syllables, the word prastâva has three syllables: that is equal (sama).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The word âdi (first, Om) has two syllables, the word pratihâra has four syllables. Taking one syllable from that over, that is equal (sama).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The word udgîtha has three syllables, the word upadrava has four syllables. With three and three syllables it should be equal. One syllable being left over, it becomes trisyllabic. Hence it is equal.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The word nidhana has three syllables, therefore it is equal. These make twenty-two syllables.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: With twenty-one syllables a man reaches the sun (and death), for the sun is the twenty-first from here; with the twenty-second he conquers what is beyond the sun: that is blessedness, that is freedom from grief.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He obtains here the victory over the sun (death), and there is a higher victory than the victory over the sun for him, who knowing this meditates on the sevenfold Sâman as uniform in itself, which leads beyond death, yea, which leads beyond death.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The hinkâra is mind, the prastâva speech, the udgîtha sight, the pratihâra hearing, the nidhana breath. That is the Gâyatra Sâman, as interwoven in the (five) prânas.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who thus knows this Gâyatra interwoven in the prânas, keeps his senses, reaches the full life, he lives long, becomes great with children and cattle, great by fame. The rule of him who thus meditates on the Gâyatra is, "Be not high-minded."
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The hinkâra is, he rubs (the fire-stick); the prastâva, smoke rises; the udgîtha, it burns; the pratihâra, there are glowing coals; the nidhana, it goes down; the nidhana, it is gone out. This is the Rathantara Sâman as interwoven in fire.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who thus knows this Rathantara interwoven in fire, becomes radiant and strong. He reaches the full life, he lives long, becomes great with children and cattle, great by fame. The rule is, 'Do not rinse the mouth or spit before the fire.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 1, 2. Next follows the Vâmadevya as interwoven in generation.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Rising, the sun is the hinkâra, risen, he is the prastâva, at noon he is the udgîtha, in the afternoon he is the pratihâra, setting, he is the nidhana. That is the Brihat Sâman as interwoven in the sun.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who thus knows the Brihat as interwoven in the sun, becomes refulgent and strong, he reaches the full life, he lives long, becomes great with children and cattle, great by fame. His rule is, 'Never complain of the heat of the sun.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The mists gather, that is the hinkâra; the cloud has risen, that is the prastâva; it rains, that is the udgîtha; it flashes and thunders, that is the pratihâra; it stops, that is the nidhana. That is the Vairûpa Sâman, as interwoven in Parganya, the god of rain.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who thus knows the Vairûpa as interwoven in Parganya, obtains all kinds of cattle (virûpa), he reaches the full life, he lives long, becomes great with children and cattle, great by fame. His rule is, 'Never complain of the rain.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The hinkâra is spring, the prastâva summer, the udgîtha the rainy season, the pratihâra autumn, the nidhana winter. That is the Vairâga Sâman, as interwoven in the seasons.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who thus knows the Vairâga, as interwoven in the seasons, shines (virâgati) through children, cattle, and glory of countenance. He reaches the full life, he lives long, becomes great with children and cattle, great by fame. His rule is, 'Never complain of the seasons.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The hinkâra is the earth, the prastâva the sky, the udgîtha heaven, the pratihâra the regions, the nidhana the sea. These are the Sakvari Sâmans, as interwoven in the worlds.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who thus knows the Sakvaris, as interwoven in the worlds, becomes possessed, of the worlds, he reaches the full life, he lives long, becomes great with children and cattle, great by fame. His rule is, 'Never complain of the worlds.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The hinkâra is goats, the prastâva sheep, the udgîtha cows, the pratihâra horses, the nidhana man. These are the Revati Sâmans, as interwoven in animals.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who thus knows these Revatis, as interwoven in animals, becomes rich in animals, he reaches the full life, he lives long, becomes great with children and cattle, great by fame. His rule is, 'Never complain of animals.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The hinkâra is hair, the prastâva skin, the udgîtha flesh, the pratihâra bone, the nidhana marrow. That is the Yagñâyagñîya Sâman, as interwoven in the members of the body.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who thus knows the Yagñâyagñîya, as interwoven in the members of the body, becomes possessed of strong limbs, he is not crippled in any limb, he reaches the full life, he lives long, becomes great with children and cattle, great by fame. His rule is, 'Do not eat marrow for a year,' or 'Do not eat marrow at all.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The hinkâra is fire, the prastâva air, the udgîtha the sun, the pratihâra the stars, the nidhana the moon. That is the Râgana Sâman, as interwoven in the deities.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who thus knows the Râgana, as interwoven in the deities, obtains the same world, the same happiness, the same company as the gods, he reaches the full life, he lives long, becomes great with children and cattle, great by fame. His rule is, 'Do not speak evil of the Brâhmanas.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The hinkâra is the threefold knowledge, the prastâva these three worlds, the udgîtha Agni (fire), Vâyu (air), and Âditya (sun), the pratihâra the stars, the birds, and the rays, the nidhana the serpents, Gandharvas, and fathers. That is the Sâman, as interwoven in everything.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And thus it is said in the following verse: 'There are the fivefold three (the three kinds of sacrificial knowledge, the three worlds &c. in their fivefold form, i.e. as identified with the hinkâra, the prastâva, &c), and the other forms of the Sâman. Greater than these there is nothing else besides.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who knows this, knows everything. All regions offer him gifts. His rule is, 'Let him meditate (on the Sâman), knowing that he is everything, yea, that he is everything.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The udgîtha, of which a poet said, I choose the deep sounding note of the Sâman as good for cattle, belongs to Agni; the indefinite note belongs to Pragâpati, the definite note to Soma, the soft and smooth note to Vâyu, the smooth and strong note to Indra, the heron-like note to Brihaspati, the dull note to Varuna. Let a man cultivate all of these, avoiding, however, that of Varuna.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: All vowels (svara) belong to Indra, all sibilants (ûshman) to Pragâpati, all consonants (sparsa) to Mrityu (death). If somebody should reprove him for his vowels, let him say, 'I went to Indra as my refuge (when pronouncing my vowels): he will answer thee.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And if somebody should reprove him for his sibilants, let him say, 'I went to Pragâpati as my refuge: he will smash thee.' And if somebody should reprove him for his consonants, let him say, 'I went to Mrityu as my refuge: he will reduce thee to ashes.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: All vowels are to be pronounced with voice (ghosha) and strength (bala), so that the Udgâtri may give strength to Indra. All sibilants are to be pronounced, neither as if swallowed (agrasta), nor as if thrown out (nirasta), but well opened (vivrita), so that the Udgâtri may give himself to Pragâpati. All consonants are to be pronounced slowly, and without crowding them together, so that the Udgâtri may withdraw himself from Mrityu.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: There are three branches of the law. Sacrifice, study, and charity are the first,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Austerity the second, and to dwell as a Brahmakârin in the house of a tutor, always mortifying the body in the house of a tutor, is the third. All these obtain the worlds of the blessed; but the Brahmasamstha alone (he who is firmly grounded in Brahman) obtains immortality.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Pragâpati brooded on the worlds. From them, thus brooded on, the threefold knowledge (sacrifice) issued forth. He brooded on it, and from it, thus brooded on, issued the three syllables, Bhûh, Bhuvah, Svah.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He brooded on them, and from them, thus brooded on, issued the Om. As all leaves are attached to a stalk, so is all speech (all words) attached to the Om (Brahman). Om is all this, yea, Om is all this.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The teachers of Brahman (Veda) declare, as the Prâtah-savana (morning-oblation) belongs to the Vasus, the Mâdhyandina-savana (noon-libation) to the Rudras, the third Savana (evening-libation) to the Âdityas and the Visve Devas,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Where then is the world of the sacrificer? He who does not know this, how can he perform the sacrifice? He only who knows, should perform it.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Before the beginning of the Prâtaranuvâka (matin-chant), the sacrificer, sitting down behind the household altar (gârhapatya), and looking towards the north, sings the Sâman, addressed to the Vasus:
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Open the door of the world (the earth), let us see thee, that we may rule (on earth).'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then he sacrifices, saying: 'Adoration to Agni, who dwells on the earth, who dwells in the world! Obtain that world for me, the sacrificer! That is the world for the sacrificer!'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'I (the sacrificer) shall go thither, when this life is over. Take this! (he says, in offering the libation.) Cast back the bolt!' Having said this, he rises. For him the Vasus fulfil the morning-oblation.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Before the beginning of the Mâdhyandinasavana, the noon-oblation, the sacrificer, sitting down behind the Âgnidhrîya altar, and looking towards the north, sings the Sâman, addressed to the Rudras:
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Open the door of the world (the sky), let us see thee, that we may rule wide (in the sky).'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then he sacrifices, saying: 'Adoration to Vâyu (air), who dwells in the sky, who dwells in the world. Obtain that world for me, the sacrificer! That is the world Tor the sacrificer!'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'I (the sacrificer) shall go thither, when this life is over. Take this! Cast back the bolt!' Having said this, he rises. For him the Rudras fulfil the noon-oblation.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Before the beginning of the third oblation, the sacrificer, sitting down behind the Âhavanîya altar, and looking towards the north, sings the Sâman, addressed to the Âdityas and Visve Devas:
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Open the door of the world (the heaven), let us see thee, that we may rule supreme (in heaven).' This is addressed to the Âdityas.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Next the Sâman addressed to the Visve Devas: 'Open the door of the world (heaven), let us see thee, that we may rule supreme (in heaven).'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then he sacrifices, saying: 'Adoration to the Âdityas and to the Visve Devas, who dwell in heaven, who dwell in the world. Obtain that world for me, the sacrificer!'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That is the world for the sacrificer! I (the sacrificer) shall go thither, when this life is over. Take this! Cast back the bolt!' Having said this, he rises.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: For him the Âdityas and the Visve Devas fulfil the third oblation. He who knows this, knows the full measure of the sacrifice, yea, he knows it.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The sun is indeed the honey of the Devas. The heaven is the cross-beam (from which) the sky (hangs as) a hive, and the bright vapours are the eggs of the bees.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The eastern rays of the sun are the honey-cells in front. The Rik verses are the bees, the Rig-veda (sacrifice) is the flower, the water (of the sacrificial libations) is the nectar (of the flower).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Those very Rik verses then (as bees) brooded over the Rig-veda sacrifice (the flower); and from it, thus brooded on, sprang as its (nectar) essence, fame, glory of countenance, vigour, strength, and health.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: That (essence) flowed forth and went towards the sun. And that forms what we call the red (rohita) light of the rising sun.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The southern rays of the sun are the honey-cells on the right. The Yagus verses are the bees, the Yagur-veda sacrifice is the flower, the water (of the sacrificial libations) is the nectar (of the flower).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Those very Yagus verses (as bees) brooded over the Yagur-veda sacrifice (the flower); and from it, thus brooded on, sprang as its (nectar) essence, fame, glory of countenance, vigour, strength, and health.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: That flowed forth and went towards the sun. And that forms what we call the white (sukla) light of the sun.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The western rays of the sun are the honey-cells behind. The Sâman verses are the bees, the Sâma-veda sacrifice is the flower, the water is the nectar.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Those very Sâman verses (as bees) brooded over the Sâma-veda sacrifice; and from it, thus brooded on, sprang as its (nectar) essence, fame, glory of countenance, vigour, strength, and health.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: That flowed forth and went towards the sun. And that forms what we call the dark (krishna) light of the sun.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Those very hymns of the Atharvângiras (as bees) brooded over the Itihâsa-purâna; and from it, thus brooded on, sprang as its (nectar) essence, fame, glory of countenance, vigour, strength, and health.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: That flowed forth, and went towards the sun. And that forms what we call the extreme dark (parah krishnam) light of the sun.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The upward rays of the sun are the honey-cells above. The secret doctrines are the bees, Brahman (the Om) is the flower, the water is the nectar.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Those secret doctrines (as bees) brooded over Brahman (the Om); and from it, thus brooded on, sprang as its (nectar) essence, fame, glory of countenance, brightness, vigour, strength, and health.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: That flowed forth, and went towards the sun. And that forms what seems to stir in the centre of the sun.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: These (the different colours in the sun) are the essences of the essences. For the Vedas are essences (the best things in the world); and of them (after they have assumed the form of sacrifice) these (the colours rising to the sun) are again the essences. They are the nectar of the nectar. For the Vedas are nectar (immortal), and of them these are the nectar.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: On the first of these nectars (the red light, which represents fame, glory of countenance, vigour, strength, health) the Vasus live, with Agni at their head. True, the Devas do not eat or drink, but they enjoy by seeing the nectar.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They enter into that (red) colour, and they rise from that colour.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who thus knows this nectar, becomes one of the Vasus, with Agni at their head, he sees the nectar and rejoices. And he, too, having entered that colour, rises again from that colour.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: So long as the sun rises in the east and sets in the west, so long does he follow the sovereign supremacy of the Vasus.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: On the second of these nectars the Rudras live, with Indra at their head. True, the Devas do not eat or drink, but they enjoy by seeing the nectar.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They enter into that white colour, and they rise from that colour.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who thus knows this nectar, becomes one of the Rudras, with Indra at their head, he sees the nectar and rejoices. And he, having entered that colour, rises again from that colour.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: So long as the sun rises in the east and sets in the west, twice as long does it rise in the south and set in the north; and so long does he follow the sovereign supremacy of the Rudras.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: On the third of these nectars the Âdityas live, with Varuna at their head. True, the Devas do not eat or drink, but they enjoy by seeing the nectar.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They enter into that (dark) colour, and they rise from that colour.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who thus knows this nectar, becomes one of the Âdityas, with Varuna at their head, he sees the nectar and rejoices. And he, having entered that colour, rises again from that colour.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: So long as the sun rises in the south and sets in the north, twice as long does it rise in the west and set in the east; and so long does he follow the sovereign supremacy of the Âdityas.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: On the fourth of these nectars the Maruts live, with Soma at their head. True, the Devas do not eat or drink, but they enjoy by seeing the nectar.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They enter in that (very dark) colour, and they rise from that colour.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who thus knows this nectar, becomes one of the Maruts, with Soma at their head, he sees the nectar and rejoices. And he, having entered that colour, rises again from that colour.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: So long as the sun rises in the west and sets in the east, twice as long does it rise in the north and set in the south; and so long does he follow the sovereign supremacy of the Maruts.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: On the fifth of these nectars the Sâdhyas live, with Brahman at their head. True, the Devas do not eat or drink, but they enjoy by seeing the nectar.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They enter into that colour, and they rise from that colour.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who thus knows this nectar, becomes one of the Sâdhyas, with Brahman at their head; he sees the nectar and rejoices. And he, having entered that colour, rises again from that colour.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: So long as the sun rises in the north and sets in the south, twice as long does it rise above, and set below; and so long does he follow the sovereign power of the Sâdhyas.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: When from thence he has risen upwards, he neither rises nor sets. He is alone, standing in the centre. And on this there is this verse:
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Yonder he neither rises nor sets at any time. If this is not true, ye gods, may I lose Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And indeed to him who thus knows this Brahma-upanishad (the secret doctrine of the Veda) the sun does not rise and does not set. For him there is day, once and for all;.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: This doctrine (beginning with III, 1, 1) Brahman (m. Hiranyagarbha) told to Pragâpati (Virâg), Pragâpati to Manu, Manu to his offspring (Ikshvâku, &c.) And the father told that (doctrine of) Brahman (n.) to Uddâlaka Âruni.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: A father may therefore tell that doctrine of Brahman to his eldest son, or to a worthy pupil. But no one should tell it to anybody else, even if he gave him the whole sea-girt earth, full of treasure, for this doctrine is worth more than that, yea, it is worth more.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The Gâyatrî (verse) is everything whatsoever here exists. Gâyatrî indeed is speech, for speech sings forth (gâya-ti) and protects (trâya-te) everything that here exists.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: That Gâyatrî is also the earth, for everything that here exists rests on the earth, and does not go beyond.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: That earth again is the body in man, for in it the vital airs (prânas, which are everything) rest, and do not go beyond.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: That body again in man is the heart within man, for in it the prânas (which are everything) rest, and do not go beyond.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: That Gâyatrî has four feet and is sixfold. And this is also declared by a Rik verse (Rig-veda X, 90, 3):—
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Such is the greatness of it (of Brahman, under the disguise of Gâyatrî); greater than it is the Person (purusha). His feet are all things. The immortal with three feet is in heaven (i.e. in himself).'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The Brahman which has been thus described (as immortal with three feet in heaven, and as Gâyatrî) is the same as the ether which is around us;
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And the ether which is around us, is the same as the ether which is within us. And the ether which is within us,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: That is the ether within the heart. That ether in the heart (as Brahman) is omnipresent and unchanging. He who knows this obtains omnipresent and unchangeable happiness.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: For that heart there are five gates belonging to the Devas (the senses). The eastern gate is the Prâna (up-breathing), that is the eye, that is Âditya (the sun). Let a man meditate on that as brightness (glory of countenance) and health. He who knows, this, becomes bright and healthy.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The southern gate is the Vyâna (back-breathing), that is the ear, that is the moon. Let a man meditate on that as happiness and fame. He who knows this, becomes happy and famous.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The western gate is the Apâna (down-breathing), that is speech, that is Agni (fire). Let a man meditate on that as glory of countenance and health. He who knows this, becomes glorious and healthy.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The northern gate is the Samâna (on-breathing), that is mind, that is Parganya (rain). Let a man meditate on that as celebrity and beauty. He who knows this, becomes celebrated and beautiful.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The upper gate is the Udâna (out-breathing), that is air, that is ether. Let a man meditate on that as strength and greatness. He who knows this, becomes strong and great.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: These are the five men of Brahman, the door-keepers of the Svarga (heaven) world. He who knows these five men of Brahman, the door-keepers of the Svarga world, in his family a strong son is born. He who thus knows these five men of Brahman, as the door-keepers of the Svarga world, enters himself the Svarga world.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Now that light which shines above this heaven, higher than all, higher than everything, in the highest world, beyond which there are no other worlds, that is the same light which is within man. And of this we have this visible proof:
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Namely, when we thus perceive by touch the warmth here in the body. And of it we have this audible proof: Namely, when we thus, after stopping our ears, listen to what is like the rolling of a carriage, or the bellowing of an ox, or the sound of a burning fire (within the ears). Let a man meditate on this as the (Brahman) which is seen and heard. He who knows this, becomes conspicuous and celebrated, yea, he becomes celebrated.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: All this is Brahman (n.) Let a man meditate on that (visible world) as beginning, ending, and breathing in it (the Brahman).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Now man is a creature of will. According to what his will is in this world, so will he be when he has departed this life. Let him therefore have this will and belief:
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The intelligent, whose body is spirit, whose form is light, whose thoughts are true, whose nature is like ether (omnipresent and invisible), from whom all works, all desires, all sweet odours and tastes proceed; he who embraces all this, who never speaks, and is never surprised,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He is my self within the heart, smaller than a corn of rice, smaller than a corn of barley, smaller than a mustard seed, smaller than a canary seed or the kernel of a canary seed. He also is my self within the heart, greater than the earth, greater than the sky, greater than heaven, greater than all these worlds.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He from whom all works, all desires, all sweet odours and tastes proceed, who embraces all this, who never speaks and who is never surprised, he, my self within the heart, is that Brahman (n.) When I shall have departed from hence, I shall obtain him (that Self). He who has this faith has no doubt; thus said Sândilya, yea, thus he said.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The chest which has the sky for its circumference and the earth for its bottom, does not decay, for the quarters are its sides, and heaven its lid above. That chest is a treasury, and all things are within it.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Its eastern quarter is called Guhtû, its southern Sahamânâ, its western Râgñî, its northern Subhûtâ. The child of those quarters is Vâyu, the air, and he who knows that the air is indeed the child of the quarters, never weeps for his sons. 'I know the wind to be the child of the quarters, may I never weep for my sons.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'I turn to the imperishable chest with such and such and such.' 'I turn to the Prâna (life) with such and such and such.' 'I turn to Bhûh with such and such and such.' 'I turn to Bhuvah with such and such and such.' 'I turn to Svah with su ch and such and such.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'When I said, I turn to Prâna, then Prâna means all whatever exists here — to that I turn.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'When I said, I turn to Bhuvah, what I said is, I turn to Agni (fire), Vâyu (air), Âditya (sun).'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'When I said, I turn to Svah, what I said is, I turn to the Rig-veda, Yagur-veda, and Sâma-veda. That is what I said, yea, that is what I said.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Man is sacrifice. His (first) twenty-four years are the morning-libation. The Gâyatrî has twenty-four syllables, the morning-libation is offered with Gâyatrî hymns. The Vasus are connected with that part of the sacrifice. The Prânas (the five senses) are the Vasus, for they make all this to abide (vâsayanti).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: If anything ails him in that (early) age, let him say: 'Ye Prânas, ye Vasus, extend this my morning-libation unto the midday-libation, that I, the sacrifices may not perish in the midst of the Prânas or Vasus.' Thus he recovers from his illness, and becomes whole.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The next forty-four years are the midday-libation. The Trishtubh has forty-four syllables, the midday-libation is offered with Trishtubh hymns. The Rudras are connected with that part of it. The Prânas are the Rudras, for they make all this to cry (rodayanti).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: If anything ails him in that (second) age, let him say: 'Ye Prânas, ye Rudras, extend this my midday-libation unto the third libation, that I, the sacrificer, may not perish in the midst of the Prânas or Rudras.' Thus he recovers from his illness, and becomes whole.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The next forty-eight years are the third libation. The Gagatî has forty-eight syllables, the third libation is offered with Gagatî hymns. The Âdityas are connected with that part of it. The Prânas are the Âdityas, for they take up all this (âdadate).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: If anything ails him in that (third) age, let him say: 'Ye Prânas, ye Âdityas, extend this my third libation unto the full age, that I, the sacrificer, may not perish in the midst of the Prânas or Âdityas.' Thus he recovers from his illness, and becomes whole.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Mahidâsa Aitareya (the son of Itarâ), who knew this, said (addressing a disease): 'Why dost thou afflict me, as I shall not die by it?' He lived a hundred and sixteen years (i.e. 24+44+48). He, too, who knows this lives on to a hundred and sixteen years.
