verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: When a man (who is the sacrificer) hungers, thirsts, and abstains from pleasures, that is the Dikshâ (initiatory rite).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: When a man eats, drinks, and enjoys pleasures, he does it with the Upasadas (the sacrificial days on which the sacrificer is allowed to partake of food).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: When a man laughs, eats, and delights himself, he does it with the Stuta-sastras (hymns sung and recited at the sacrifices).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Penance, liberality, righteousness, kindness, truthfulness, these form his Dakshinâs (gifts bestowed on priests, &c.)
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Therefore when they say, 'There will be a birth,' and 'there has been a birth' (words used at the Soma-sacrifice, and really meaning, 'He will pour out the Soma-juice,' and 'he has poured out the Soma-juice'), that is his new birth. His death is the Avabhritha ceremony (when the sacrificial vessels are carried away to be cleansed).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Ghora Ângirasa, after having communicated this (view of the sacrifice) to Krishna, the son of Devaki— and he never thirsted again (after other knowledge)— said: "Let a man, when his end approaches, take refuge with this Triad:'Thou art the imperishable;' 'Thou art the unchangeable,' 'Thou art the edge of Prâna.' On this subject there are two Rik verses (Rig-veda VIII, 6, 30):—
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Then they see (within themselves) the everpresent light of the old seed (of the world, the Sat), the highest, which is lighted in the brilliant (Brahman)." Rig-veda I, 50, 10:—
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Perceiving above the darkness (of ignorance) the higher light (in the sun), as the higher light within the heart, the bright source (of light and life) among the gods, we have reached the highest light, yea, the highest light.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Let a man meditate on mind as Brahman (n.), this is said with reference to the body. Let a man meditate on the ether as Brahman (n.), this is said with reference to the Devas. Thus both the meditation which has reference to the body, and the meditation which has reference to the Devas, has been taught.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Speech is indeed the fourth foot of Brahman. That foot shines with Agni (fire) as its light, and warms. He who knows this, shines and warms through his celebrity, fame, and glory of countenance.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Breath is indeed the fourth foot of Brahman. That foot shines with Vâyu (air) as its light, and warms. He who knows this, shines and warms through his celebrity, fame, and glory of countenance.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The eye is indeed the fourth foot of Brahman. That foot shines with Âditya (sun) as its light, and warms. He who knows this, shines and warms through his celebrity, fame, and glory of countenance.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The ear is indeed the fourth foot of Brahman. That foot shines with the quarters as its light, and warms. He who knows this, shines and warms through his celebrity, fame, and glory of countenance.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Âditya (the sun) is Brahman, this is the doctrine, and this is the fuller account of it:—
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: In the beginning this was non-existent. It
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: became existent, it grew. It turned into an egg . The egg lay for the time of a year. The egg broke open. The two halves were one of silver, the other of gold.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The silver one became this earth, the golden one the sky, the thick membrane (of the white) the mountains, the thin membrane (of the yoke) the mist with the clouds, the small veins the rivers, the fluid the sea.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And what was born from it that was Âditya, the sun. When he was born shouts of hurrah arose, and all beings arose, and all things which they desired. Therefore whenever the sun rises and sets, shouts of hurrah arise, and all beings arise, and all things which they desire.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: If any one knowing this meditates on the sun as Brahman, pleasant shouts will approach him and will continue, yea, they will continue.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: There lived once upon a time Gânasruti Pautrâyana (the great-grandson of Ganasruta), who was a pious giver, bestowing much wealth upon the people, and always keeping open house. He built places of refuge everywhere, wishing that people should everywhere eat of his food.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Once in the night some Hamsas (flamingoes) flew over his house, and one flamingo said to another: 'Hey, Bhallâksha, Bhallâksha (short-sighted friend). The light (glory) of Gânasruti Pautrâyana has spread like the sky. Do not go near, that it may not burn thee.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The other answered him: 'How can you speak of him, being what he is (a râganya, noble), as if he were like Raikva with the car?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The first replied: 'How is it with this Raikva with the car of whom thou speakest?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The other answered: 'As (in a game of dice) all the lower casts belong to him who has conquered with the Krita cast, so whatever good deeds other people perform, belong to that Raikva. He who knows what he knows, he is thus spoken of by me.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Gânasruti Pautrâyana overheard this conversation, and as soon as he had risen in the morning, he said to his door keeper (kshattri): 'Friend, dost thou speak of (me, as if I were) Raikva with the car?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He replied: 'How is it with this Raikva with the car?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The door-keeper went to look for Raikva, but returned saying, 'I found him not.' Then the king said: 'Alas! where a Brâhmana should be searched for (in the solitude of the forest), there go for him.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The door-keeper came to a man who was lying beneath a car and scratching his sores. He addressed him, and said: 'Sir, are you Raikva with the car?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He answered: 'Here I am.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then the door-keeper returned, and said: I have found him.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then Gânasruti Pautrâyana took six hundred cows, a necklace, and a carriage with mules, went to Raikva and said:
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Raikva, here are six hundred cows, a necklace, and a carriage with mules; teach me the deity which you worship.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The other replied: 'Fie, necklace and carriage be thine, O Sûdra, together with the cows.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then Gânasruti Pautrâyana took again a thousand cows, a necklace, a carriage with mules, and his own daughter, and went to him.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said to him: 'Raikva, there are a thousand cows, a necklace, a carriage with mules, this wife, and this village in which thou dwellest. Sir, teach me!'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He, opening her mouth, said: 'You have brought these (cows and other presents), O Sûdra, but only by that mouth did you make me speak.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: These are the Raikva-parana villages in the country of the Mahâvrishas (mahâpunyas) where Raikva dwelt under him. And he said to him:
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Air (vâyu) is indeed the end of all. For when fire goes out, it goes into air. When the sun goes down, it goes into air. When the moon goes down, it goes into air.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'When water dries up, it goes into air. Air indeed consumes them all. So much with reference to the Devas.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Now with reference to the body. Breath (prâna) is indeed the end of all. When a man sleeps, speech goes into breath, so do sight, hearing, and mind. Breath indeed consumes them all.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'These are the two ends, air among the Devas, breath among the senses (prâna).'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Once while Saunaka Kâpeya and Abhipratârin Kâkshaseni were being waited on at their meal, a religious student begged of them. They gave him nothing.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said; 'One god— who is he?— swallowed the four great ones, he, the guardian of the world. O Kâpeya, mortals see him not, O Abhipratârin, though he dwells in many places. He to whom this food belongs, to him it has not been given.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Saunaka Kâpeya, pondering on that speech, went to the student and said: 'He is the self of the Devas, the creator of all beings, with golden tusks, the eater, not without intelligence. His greatness is said to be great indeed, because, without being eaten, he eats even what is not food. Thus do we, O Brahmakârin, meditate on that Being.' Then he said: 'Give him food.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They gave him food. Now these five (the eater Vâyu (air), and his food, Agni (fire), Âditya (sun), Kandramas (moon), Ap (water)) and the other five (the eater Prâna (breath), and his food, speech, sight, hearing, mind) make ten, and that is the Krita. (the highest) cast (representing the ten, the eaters and the food). Therefore in all quarters those ten are food (and) Krita. (the highest cast). These are again the Virâg (of ten syllables) which eats the food. Through this all this becomes seen. He who knows this sees all this and becomes an eater of food, yea, he becomes an eater of food.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Satyakâma, the son of Gabâlâ, addressed his mother and said: 'I wish to become a Brahmakârin (religious student), mother. Of what family am I?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: She said to him: 'I do not know, my child, of what family thou art. In my youth when I had to move about much as a servant (waiting on the guests in my father's house), I conceived thee. I do not know of what family thou art. I am Gabâlâ by name, thou art Satyakâma (Philalethes). Say that thou art Satyakâma Gabâlâ.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He going to Gautama Hâridrumata said to him, 'I wish to become a Brahmakârin with you, Sir. May I come to you, Sir?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said to him: 'Of what family are you, my friend?' He replied: 'I do not know, Sir, of what family I am. I asked my mother, and she answered: 'In my youth when I had to move about much as a servant, I conceived thee. I do not know of what family thou art. I am Gabâlâ by name, thou art Satyakâma,' I am therefore Satyakâma Gabâlâ, Sir.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said to him: 'No one but a true Brâhmana would thus speak out. Go and fetch fuel, friend, I shall initiate you. You have not swerved from the truth.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Having initiated him, he chose four hundred lean and weak cows, and said: 'Tend these, friend.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He drove them out and said to himself, 'I shall not return unless I bring back a thousand.' He dwelt a number of years (in the forest), and when the cows had become a thousand,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The bull of the herd (meant for Vâyu) said to him: 'Satyakâma!' He replied: 'Sir!' The bull said: 'We have become a thousand, lead us to the house of the teacher;
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Declare it, Sir,' he replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said to him; 'The eastern region is one quarter, the western region is one quarter, the southern region is one quarter, the northern region is one quarter. This is a foot of Brahman, consisting of the four quarters, and called Prakâsavat (endowed with splendour).'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who knows this and meditates on the foot of Brahman, consisting of four quarters, by the name of Prakâsavat, becomes endowed with splendour in this world. He conquers the resplendent worlds, whoever knows this and meditates on the foot of Brahman, consisting of the four quarters, by the name of Prakâsavat.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: (After these words of the bull), Satyakâma, on the morrow, drove the cows (toward the house of the teacher). And when they came towards the evening, he lighted a fire, penned the cows, laid wood on the fire, and sat down behind the fire, looking to the east.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then Agni (the fire) said to him: 'Satyakâma!' He replied: 'Sir.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Agni said: 'Friend, I will declare unto you one foot of Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Declare it, Sir,' he replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said to him: 'The earth is one quarter, the sky is one quarter, the heaven is one quarter, the ocean is one quarter. This is a foot of Brahman, consisting of four quarters, and called Anantavat (endless).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who knows this and meditates on the foot of Brahman, consisting of four quarters, by the name of Anantavat, becomes endless in this world. He conquers the endless worlds, whoever knows this and meditates on the foot of Brahman, consisting of four quarters, by the name of Anantavat.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'A Hamsa (flamingo, meant for the sun) will declare to you another foot of Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: (After these words of Agni), Satyakâma, on the morrow, drove the cows onward. And when they came towards the evening, he lighted a fire, penned the cows, laid wood on the fire, and sat down behind the fire, looking toward the east.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then a Hamsa flew near and said to him: 'Satyakima.' He replied: 'Sir.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The Hamsa said: 'Friend, I will declare unto you one foot of Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Declare it, Sir,' he replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said to him: 'Fire is one quarter, the sun is one quarter, the moon is one quarter, lightning is one quarter. This is a foot of Brahman, consisting of four quarters, and called Gyotishmat (full of light).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who knows this and meditates on the foot of Brahman, consisting of four quarters, by the name of Gyotishmat, becomes full of light in this world. He conquers the worlds which are full of light, whoever knows this and meditates on the foot of Brahman, consisting of four quarters, by the name of Gyotishmat.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'A diver-bird (Madgu, meant for Prâna) will declare to you another foot of Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: (After these words of the Hamsa), Satyakâma, on the morrow, drove the cows onward. And when they came towards the evening, he lighted a fire, penned the cows, laid wood on the fire, and sat down behind the fire, looking toward the east.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then a diver flew near and said to him: 'Satyakâma.' He replied: 'Sir.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The diver said: 'Friend, I will declare unto you one foot of Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Declare it, Sir,' he replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said to him: 'Breath is one quarter, the eye is one quarter, the ear is one quarter, the mind is one quarter. This is a foot of Brahman, consisting of four quarters, and called Âyatanavat (having a home).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who knows this and meditates on the foot of Brahman, consisting of four quarters, by the name of Âyatanavat, becomes possessed of a home in this world. He conquers the worlds which offer a home, whoever knows this and meditates on the foot of Brahman, consisting of four quarters, by the name of Âyatanavat.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Thus he reached the house of his teacher. The teacher said to him: 'Satyakâma.' He replied: 'Sir.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The teacher said: 'Friend, you shine like one who knows Brahman. Who then has taught you?' He replied: 'Not men. But you only, Sir, I wish, should teach me;
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'For I have heard from men like you, Sir, that only knowledge which is learnt from a teacher (Âkârya), leads to real good.' Then he taught him the same knowledge. Nothing was left out, yea, nothing was left out.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Upakosala Kâmalâyana dwelt as a Brahmakârin (religious student) in the house of Satyakâma Gâbâla. He tended his fires for twelve years. But the teacher, though he allowed other pupils (after they had learnt the sacred books) to depart to their own homes, did not allow Upakosala to depart.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then his wife said to him: 'This student, who is quite exhausted (with austerities), has carefully tended your fires. Let not the fires themselves blame you, but teach him.' The teacher, however, went away on a journey without having taught him.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The student from sorrow was not able to eat. Then the wife of the teacher said to him: 'Student, eat! Why do you not eat?' He said: 'There are many desires in this man here, which lose themselves in different directions. I am full of sorrows, and shall take no food.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Thereupon the fires said among themselves: 'This student, who is quite exhausted, has carefully tended us. Well, let us teach him.' They said to him:
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Breath is Brahman, Ka (pleasure) is Brahman, Kha (ether) is Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said: 'I understand that breath is Brahman, but I do not understand Ka or Kha.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They said: 'What is Ka is Kha, what is Kha is Ka.' They therefore taught him Brahman as breath, and as the ether (in the heart).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: After that the Gârhapatya fire taught him: 'Earth, fire, food, and the sun (these are my forms, or forms of Brahman). The person that is seen in the sun, I am he, I am he indeed.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who knowing this meditates on him, destroys sin, obtains the world (of Agni Gârhapatya), reaches his full age, and lives long; his descendants do not perish. We guard him in this world and in the other; whosoever knowing this meditates on him.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then the Anvâhârya fire taught him: 'Water, the quarters, the stars, the moon (these are my forms). The person that is seen in the moon, I am he, I am he indeed.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who knowing this meditates on him, destroys sin, obtains the world (of Agni Anvâhârya), reaches his full age, and lives long; his descendants do not perish. We guard him in this world and in the other, whosoever knowing this meditates on him.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who knowing this meditates on him, destroys sin, obtains the world (of Agni Âhavanîya), reaches his full age, and lives long; his descendants do not perish. We guard him in this world and in the other, whosoever knowing this meditates on him.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then they all said: 'Upakosala, this is our knowledge, our friend, and the knowledge of the Self, but the teacher will tell you the way (to another life).'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: In time his teacher came back, and said to him: 'Upakosala.' He answered: 'Sir.' The teacher said: 'Friend, your face shines like that of one who knows Brahman. Who has taught you?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Who should teach me, Sir?' he said. He denies, as it were. And he said (pointing) to the fires: 'Are these fires other than fires?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The teacher said: 'What, my friend, have these fires told you?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He answered: 'This' (repeating some of what they had told him).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The teacher said: 'My friend, they have taught you about the worlds, but I shall tell you this; and as water does not cling to a lotus leaf, so no evil deed clings to one who knows it.' He said: 'Sir, tell it me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said: 'The person that is seen in the eye, that is the Self. This is the immortal, the fearless, this is Brahman. Even though they drop melted butter or water on him, it runs away on both sides.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'They call him Samyadvâma, for all blessings (vâma) go towards him (samyanti). All blessings go towards him who knows this.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He is also Vâmanî, for he leads (nayati) all blessings (vâma). He leads all blessings who knows this.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He is also Bhâmanî, for he shines (bhâti) in all worlds. He who knows this, shines in all worlds.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Now (if one who knows this, dies), whether people perform obsequies for him or no, he goes to light (arkis), from light to day, from day to the light half of the moon, from the light half of the moon to the six months during which the sun goes to the north, from the months to the year, from the year to the sun, from the sun to the moon, from the moon to the lightning. There is a person not human,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He leads them to Brahman. This is the path of the Devas, the path that leads to Brahman. Those who proceed on that path, do not return to the life of man, yea, they do not return.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Verily, he who purifies (Vâyu) is the sacrifice, for he (the air) moving along, purifies everything. Because moving along he purifies everything, therefore he is the sacrifice. Of that sacrifice there are two ways, by mind and by speech.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The Brahman priest performs one of them in his mind, the Hotri, Adhvaryu, and Udgâtri priests perform the other by words. When the Brahman priest, after the Prâtaranuvâka ceremony has begun, but before the recitation of the Paridhânîyâ hymn, has (to break his silence and) to speak,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He performs perfectly the one way only (that by words), but the other is injured. As a man walking on one foot, or a carriage going on one wheel, is injured, his sacrifice is injured, and with the injured sacrifice the sacrificer is injured; yes, having sacrificed, he becomes worse.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: But when after the Prâtaranuvâka ceremony has begun and before the recitation of the Paridhânlyâ hymn, the Brahman priest has not (to break his silence and) to speak, they perform both ways perfectly, and neither of them is injured.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: As a man walking on two legs and a carriage going on two wheels gets on, so his sacrifice gets on, and with the successful sacrifice the sacrificer gets on; yes, having sacrificed, he becomes better.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Pragâpati brooded over the worlds, and from them thus brooded on he squeezed out the essences, Agni (fire) from the earth, Vâyu (air) from the sky, Âditya (the sun) from heaven.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He brooded over these three deities, and from them thus brooded on he squeezed out the essences, the Rik verses from Agni, the Yagus verses from Vâyu, the Sâman verses from Âditya.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He brooded over the threefold knowledge (the three Vedas), and from it thus brooded on he squeezed out the essences, the sacred interjection Bhûs from the Rik verses, the sacred interjection Bhuvas from the Yagus verses, the sacred interjection Svar from the Sâman verses.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: If the sacrifice is injured from the Rig-veda side, let him offer a libation in the Gârhapatya fire, saying, Bhûh, Svâha! Thus does he bind together and heal, by means of the essence and the power of the Rik verses themselves, whatever break the Rik sacrifice may have suffered.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: If the sacrifice is injured from the Yagur-veda side, let him offer a libation in the Dakshina fire, saying, Bhuvah, Svâhâ! Thus does he bind together and heal, by means of the essence and the power of the Yagus verses themselves, whatever break the Yagus sacrifice may have suffered.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: As one binds (softens) gold by means of lavana (borax), and silver by means of gold, and tin by means of silver, and lead by means of tin, and iron (loha) by means of lead, and wood by means of iron, or also by means of leather,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Thus does one bind together and heal any break in the sacrifice by means of (the Vyâhritis or sacrificial interjections which are) the essence and strength of the three worlds, of the deities, and of the threefold knowledge. That sacrifice is healed in which there is a Brahman priest who knows this.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: That sacrifice is inclined towards the north (in the right way) in which there is a Brahman priest who knows this. And with regard to such a Brahman priest there is the following Gâthâ: 'Wherever it falls back, thither the man goes,'— viz. the Brahman only, as one of the Ritvig priests. 'He saves the Kurus as a mare' (viz. a Brahman priest who knows this, saves the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and all the other priests). Therefore let a man make him who knows this his Brahman priest, not one who does not know it, who does not know it.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who knows the oldest and the best becomes himself the oldest and the best. Breath indeed is the oldest and the best.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who knows the richest, becomes himself the richest. Speech indeed is the richest.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who knows the firm rest, becomes himself firm in this world and in the next. The eye indeed is the firm rest.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who knows success, his wishes succeed, both his divine and human wishes. The ear indeed is success.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who knows the home, becomes a home of his people. The mind indeed is the home.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They went to their father Pragâpati and said: 'Sir, who is the best of us?' He replied: 'He by whose departure the body seems worse than worst, he is the best of you.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The tongue (speech) departed, and having been absent for a year, it came round and said: 'How have you been able to live without me?' They replied: 'Like mute people, not speaking, but breathing with the breath, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear, thinking with the mind. Thus we lived.' Then speech went back.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The eye (sight) departed, and having been absent for a year, it came round and said: 'How have you been able to live without me?' They replied: 'Like blind people, not seeing, but breathing with the breath, speaking with the tongue, hearing with the ear, thinking with the mind. Thus we lived.' Then the eye went back.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The ear (hearing) departed, and having been absent for a year, it came round and said: 'How have you been able to live without me?' They replied: 'Like deaf people, not hearing, but breathing with the breath, speaking with the tongue, thinking with the mind. Thus we lived.' Then the ear went back.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The mind departed, and having been absent for a year, it came round and said: 'How have you been able to live without me?' They replied: 'Like children whose mind is not yet formed, but breathing with the breath, speaking with the tongue, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear. Thus we lived.' Then the mind went back.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The breath, when on the point of departing, tore up the other senses, as a horse, going to start, might tear up the pegs to which he is tethered. They came to him and said: 'Sir, be thou (our lord); thou art the best among us. Do not depart from us!'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then the tongue said to him: 'If I am the richest, thou art the richest.' The eye said to him: 'If I am the firm rest, thou art the firm rest.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The ear said to him: 'If I am success, thou art success.' The mind said to him: 'If I am the home, thou art the home.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And people do not call them, the tongues, the eyes, the ears, the minds, but the breaths (prâna, the senses). For breath are all these.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Breath said: 'What shall be my food?' They answered: 'Whatever there is, even unto dogs and birds.' Therefore this is food for Ana (the breather). His name is clearly Ana. To him who knows this there is nothing that is not (proper) food.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Satyakâma Gâbâla, after he had communicated this to Gosruti Vaiyâghrapadya, said to him: 'If you were to tell this to a dry stick, branches would grow, and leaves spring from it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: If a man wishes to reach greatness, let him perform the Dîkshâ (preparatory rite) on the day of the new moon, and then, on the night of the full moon, let him stir a mash of all kinds of herbs with curds and honey, and let him pour ghee on the fire (âvasathya laukika), saying, 'Svâhâ to the oldest and the best.' After that let him throw all that remains (of the ghee) into the mash.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: In the same manner let him pour ghee on the fire, saying, 'Svâhâ to the richest.' After that let him throw all that remains together into the mash.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: In the same manner let him pour ghee on the fire, saying, 'Svâhâ to the firm rest.' After that let him throw all that remains together into the mash. In the same manner let him pour ghee on the fire, saying, 'Svâhâ to success.' After that let him throw all that remains together into the mash.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then going forward and placing the mash in his hands, he recites: 'Thou (Prâna) art Ama by name, for all this together exists in thee. He is the oldest and best, the king, the sovereign. May he make me the oldest, the best, the king, the sovereign. May I be all this.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then he eats with the following Rik verse at every foot: 'We choose that food'—here he swallows—'Of the divine Savitri (prâna)'—here he swallows—'The best and all-supporting food'— here he swallows — "We meditate on the speed of Bhaga (Savitri, prâna)'—here he drinks all.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Having cleansed the vessel, whether it be a kamsa or a kamasa, he sits down behind the fire on a skin or on the bare ground, without speaking or making any other effort. If in his dream he sees a woman, let him know this to be a sign that his sacrifice has succeeded.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: On this there is a Sloka: 'If during sacrifices which are to fulfil certain wishes he sees in his dreams a woman, let him know success from this vision in a dream, yea, from this vision in a dream.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Svetaketu Âruneya went to an assembly of the Pañkâlas. Pravâhana Gaivali said to him: 'Boy, has your father instructed you?' 'Yes, Sir,' he replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Do you know to what place men go from here?' 'No, Sir,' he replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Do you know how they return again?' 'No Sir,' he replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Do you know where the path of Devas and the path of the fathers diverge?' 'No, Sir,' he replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: "Do you know why that world never becomes full?' 'No, Sir," he replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Do you know why in the fifth libation water is called Man?' 'No, Sir,' he replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Then why did you say (you had been) instructed? How could anybody who did not know these things say that he had been instructed?' Then the boy went back sorrowful to the place of his father, and said: 'Though you had not instructed me, Sir, you said you had instructed me.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That fellow of a Râganya asked me five questions, and I could not answer one of them.' The father said: 'As you have told me these questions of his, I do not know any one of them. If I knew these questions, how should I not have told you?
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then Gautama went to the kings place, and when he had come to him, the king offered him proper respect. In the morning the king went out on his way to the assembly. The king said to him: 'Sir, Gautama, ask a boon of such things as men possess.' He replied: 'Such things as men possess may remain with you. Tell me the speech which you addressed to the boy.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The king was perplexed, and commanded him, saying: 'Stay with me some time.' Then he said: 'As (to what) you have said to me, Gautama, this knowledge did not go to any Brâhmana before you, and therefore this teaching belonged in all the worlds to the Kshatra class alone. Then he began:
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'The altar (on which the sacrifice is supposed to be offered) is that world (heaven), O Gautama; its fuel is the sun itself, the smoke his rays, the light the day, the coals the moon, the sparks the stars.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'On that altar the Devas (or prânas, represented by Agni, &c.) offer the sraddhâ libation (consisting of water). From that oblation rises Soma, the king (the moon).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'On that altar the Devas offer Soma, the king (the moon). From that oblation rises rain.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'The altar is the earth, O Gautama; its fuel is the year itself, the smoke the ether, the light the night, the coals the quarters, the sparks the intermediate quarters.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'On that altar the Devas (prânas) offer rain. From that oblation rises food (corn, &c.)
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'The altar is man, O Gautama; its fuel speech itself, the smoke the breath, the light the tongue, the coals the eye, the sparks the ear.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'On that altar the Devas (prânas) offer food. From that oblation rises seed.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'The altar is woman, O Gautama.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'On that altar the Devas (prânas) offer seed. From that oblation rises the germ.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'For this reason is water in the fifth oblation called Man. This germ, covered in the womb, having dwelt there ten months, or more or less, is born.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'When born, he lives whatever the length of his life may be. When he has departed, his friends carry him, as appointed, to the fire (of the funeral pile) from whence he came, from whence he sprang.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Those who know this (even though they still be grihasthas, householders) and those who in the forest follow faith and austerities (the vânaprasthas, and of the parivrâgakas those who do not yet know the Highest Brahman) go to light (arkis), from light to day, from day to the light half of the moon, from the light half of the moon to the six months when the sun goes to the north, from the six months when the sun goes to the north to the year, from the year to the sun, from the sun to the moon, from the moon to the lightning. There is a person not human,—
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He leads them to Brahman (the conditioned Brahman). This is the path of the Devas.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'But they who living in a village practise (a life of) sacrifices, works of public utility, and alms, they go to the smoke, from smoke to night, from night to the dark half of the moon, from the dark half of the moon to the six months when the sun goes to the south. But they do not reach the year.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Having dwelt there, till their (good) works are consumed, they return again that way as they came, to the ether, from the ether to the air. Then the sacrificer, having become air, becomes smoke, having become smoke, he becomes mist,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Those whose conduct has been good, will quickly attain some good birth, the birth of a Brâhmana, or a Kshatriya, or a Vaisya. But those whose conduct has been evil, will quickly attain an evil birth, the birth of a dog, or a hog, or a Kandâla.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'On neither of these two ways those small creatures (flies, worms, &c.) are continually returning of whom it may be said, Live and die. Theirs is a third place.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Therefore that world never becomes full (cf. V, 3, 2).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Hence let a man take care to himself! And thus
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: it is said in the following Sloka:—
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'A man who steals gold, who drinks spirits, who dishonours his Guru's bed, who kills a Brahman, these four fall, and as a fifth he who associates with them.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'But he who thus knows the five fires is not defiled by sin even though he associates with them. He who knows this, is pure, clean, and obtains the world of the blessed, yea, he obtains the world of the blessed.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Prâkînasâla Aupamanyava, Satyayagña Paulushi, Indradyumna Bhâllaveya, Gana Sârkarâkshya, and Budila Âsvatarasvi, these five great householders and great theologians came once together and held a discussion as to What is our Self, and what is Brahman.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They reflected and said: 'Sirs, there is that Uddâlaka Âruni, who knows at present that Self, called Vaisvânara. Well, let us go to him.' They went to him.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: But he reflected: 'Those great householders and great theologians will examine me, and I shall not be able to tell them all; therefore I shall recommend another teacher to them.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said to them: 'Sirs, Asvapati Kaikeya knows at present that Self, called Vaisvânara. Well, let us go to him.' They went to him.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: When they arrived (the king) ordered proper presents to be made separately to each of them. And rising the next morning he said: 'In my kingdom there is no thief, no miser, no drunkard, no man without an altar in his house, no ignorant person, no adulterer, much less an adulteress. I am going to perform a sacrifice, Sirs, and as much wealth as I give to each Ritvig priest, I shall give to you, Sirs. Please to stay here.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They replied: 'Every man ought to say for what purpose he comes. You know at present that Vaisvânara Self, tell us that.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said: 'To-morrow I shall give you an answer.' Therefore on the next morning they approached him, carrying fuel in their hands (like students), and he, without first demanding any preparatory rites, said to them:
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Aupamanyava, whom do you meditate on as the Self?' He replied: 'Heaven only, venerable king.' He said: 'The Self which you meditate on is the Vaisvânara Self, called Sutegas (having good light). Therefore every kind of Soma libation is seen in your house.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'You eat food, and see your desire (a son, &c), and whoever thus meditates on that Vaisvânara Self, eats food, sees his desire, and has Vedic glory (arising from study and sacrifice) in his house. That, however, is but the head of the Self, and thus your head would have fallen (in a discussion), if you had not come to me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then he said to Satyayagña Paulushi: 'O Prâkînayogya, whom do you meditate on as the Self?' He replied: 'The sun only, venerable king.' He said: 'The Self which you meditate on is the Vaisvânara Self, called Visvarûpa (multiform). Therefore much and manifold wealth is seen in your house.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'There is a car with mules, full of slaves and jewels. You eat food and see your desire, and whoever thus meditates on that Vaisvânara Self, eats food and sees his desire, and has Vedic glory in his house.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That, however, is but the eye of the Self, and you would have become blind, if you had not come to me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then he said to Indradyumna Bhâllaveya: 'O Vaiyâghrapadya, whom do you meditate on as the Self?' He replied: 'Air only, venerable king.' He said: 'The Self which you meditate on is the Vaisvânara Self, called Prithagvartman (having various courses). Therefore offerings come to you in various ways, and rows of cars follow you in various ways.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'You eat food and see your desire, and whoever thus meditates on that Vaisvânara Self, eats food and sees his desire, and has Vedic glory in his house.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That, however, is but the breath of the Self, and your breath would have left you, if you had not come to me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then he said to Gana Sârkarâkshya: 'Whom do you meditate on as the Self?' He replied: 'Ether only, venerable king.' He said: 'The Self which you meditate on is the Vaisvânara Self, called Bahula (full). Therefore you are full of offspring and wealth.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'You eat food and see your desire, and whoever thus meditates on that Vaisvânara Self, eats food and sees his desire, and has Vedic glory in his house.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: That, however, is but the trunk of the Self, and your trunk would have perished, if you had not come to me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then he said to Budila Âsvatarâsvi, 'O Vaiyâghrapadya, whom do you meditate on as the Self?' He replied: 'Water only, venerable king.' He said: 'The Self which you meditate on is the Vaisvânara Self, called Rayi (wealth). Therefore are you wealthy and flourishing.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'You eat food and see your desire, and whoever thus meditates on that Vaisvânara Self, eats food and sees his desire, and has Vedic glory in his house.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That, however, is but the bladder of the Self, and your bladder would have burst, if you had not come to me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then he said to Auddâlaka Âruni: 'O Gautama, whom do you meditate on as the Self?' He replied: 'The earth only, venerable king.' He said: 'The Self which you meditate on is the Vaisvânara Self, called Pratishthâ (firm rest). Therefore you stand firm with offspring and cattle.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'You eat food and see your desire, and whoever thus meditates on that Vaisvânara Self, eats food and sees his desire, and has Vedic glory in his house.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That, however, are but the feet of the Self, and your feet would have given way, if you had not come to me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then he said to them all: 'You eat your food, knowing that Vaisvânara Self as if it were many. But he who worships the Vaisvânara Self as a span long, and as identical with himself, he eats food in all worlds, in all beings, in all Selfs.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Of that Vaisvânara Self the head is Sutegas (having good light), the eye Visvarûpa (multiform), the breath Prithagvartman (having various courses), the trunk Bahula (full), the bladder Rayi (wealth), the feet the earth, the chest the altar, the hairs the grass on the altar, the heart the Gârhapatya fire, the mind the Anvâhârya fire, the mouth the Âhavanîya fire.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Therefore the first food which a man may take, is in the place of Homa. And he who offers that first oblation, should offer it to Prâna (up-breathing), saying Svâhâ. Then Prâna (up-breathing) is satisfied,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'If Prâna is satisfied, the eye is satisfied, if the eye is satisfied, the sun is satisfied, if the sun is satisfied, heaven is satisfied, if heaven is satisfied, whatever is under heaven and under the sun is satisfied. And through their satisfaction he (the sacrificer or eater) himself is satisfied with offspring, cattle, health, brightness, and Vedic splendour.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And he who offers the second oblation, should offer it to Vyâna (back-breathing), saying Svâhâ. Then Vyina is satisfied,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'If Vyâna is satisfied, the ear is satisfied, if the ear is satisfied, the moon is satisfied, if the moon is satisfied, the quarters are satisfied, if the quarters are satisfied, whatever is under the quarters and under the moon is satisfied. And through their satisfaction he (the sacrificer or eater) himself is satisfied with offspring, cattle, health, brightness, and Vedic splendour.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And he who offers the third oblation, should offer it to Apâna (down-breathing), saying Svâhâ. Then Apâna is satisfied. If Apâna is satisfied, the tongue is satisfied, if the tongue is satisfied, Agni (fire) is satisfied, if Agni is satisfied, the earth is satisfied, if the earth is satisfied, whatever is under the earth and under fire is satisfied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And through their satisfaction he (the sacrificer or eater) himself is satisfied with offspring, cattle, health, brightness, and Vedic splendour.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And he who offers the fourth oblation, should offer it to Samâna (on-breathing), saying Svâhâ. Then Samâna is satisfied,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'If Samâna is satisfied, the mind is satisfied, if the mind is satisfied, Parganya (god of rain) is satisfied, if Parganya is satisfied, lightning is satisfied, if lightning is satisfied, whatever is under Parganya and under lightning is satisfied. And through their satisfaction he (the sacrificer or eater) himself is satisfied with offspring, cattle, health, brightness, and Vedic splendour.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And he who offers the fifth oblation, should offer it to Udâna (out-breathing), saying Svâhâ. Then Udâna is satisfied,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'If Udâna is satisfied, Vâyu (air) is satisfied, if Vâyu is satisfied, ether is satisfied, if ether is satisfied, whatever is under Vâyu and under the ether is satisfied. And through their satisfaction he (the sacrificer or eater) himself is satisfied with offspring, cattle, health, brightness, and Vedic splendour.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'If, without knowing this, one offers an Agnihotra, it would be as if a man were to remove the live coals and pour his libation on dead ashes.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'But he who offers this Agnihotra with a full knowledge of its true purport, he offers it (i.e. he eats food) in all worlds, in all beings, in all Selfs.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'As the soft fibres of the Ishîkâ reed, when thrown into the fire, are burnt, thus all his sins are burnt whoever offers this Agnihotra with a full knowledge of its true purport.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Even if he gives what is left of his food to a Kandâla, it would be offered in his (the Kandâla's) Vaisvânara Self. And so it is said in this Sloka:—
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'As hungry children here on earth sit (expectantly) round their mother, so do all beings sit round the Agnihotra, yea, round the Agnihotra.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Harih, Om. There lived once Svetaketu Âruneya (the grandson of Aruna). To him his father (Uddâlaka, the son of Aruna) said: 'Svetaketu, go to school; for there is none belonging to our race, darling, who, not having studied (the Veda), is, as it were, a Brâhmana by birth only.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Having begun his apprenticeship (with a teacher) when he was twelve years of age, Svetaketu returned to his father, when he was twenty-four, having then studied all the Vedas,—conceited, considering himself well-read, and stern.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: His father said to him: 'Svetaketu, as you are so conceited, considering yourself so well-read, and so stern, my dear, have you ever asked for that instruction by which we hear what cannot be heard, by which we perceive what cannot be perceived, by which we know what cannot be known?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'What is that instruction, Sir?' he asked.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The father replied: 'My dear, as by one clod of clay all that is made of clay is known, the difference being only a name, arising from speech, but the truth being that all is clay;
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And as, my dear, by one nugget of gold all that is made of gold is known, the difference being only a name, arising from speech, but the truth being that all is gold?
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And as, my dear, by one pair of nail-scissors all that is made of iron (kârshnâyasam) is known, the difference being only a name, arising from speech, but the truth being that all is iron,—thus, my dear, is that instruction.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The son said: 'Surely those venerable men (my teachers) did not know that. For if they had known it, why should they not have told it me? Do you, Sir, therefore tell me that.' 'Be it so,' said the father.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'In the beginning,' my dear, "there was that only which is (τὸ ὄν), one only, without a second. Others say, in the beginning there was that only which is not (τὸ μὴ ὄν), one only, without a second; and from that which is not, that which is was born.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'But how could it be thus, my dear?' the father continued. 'How could that which is, be born of that which is not? No, my dear, only that which is, was in the beginning, one only, without a second.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'It thought may I be many, may I grow forth. It sent forth fire.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That fire thought, may I be many, may I grow forth. It sent forth water.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And therefore whenever anybody anywhere is hot and perspires, water is produced on him from fire alone.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Water thought, may I be many, may I grow forth. It sent forth earth (food).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Therefore whenever it rains anywhere, most food is then produced. From water alone is eatable food produced.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Of all living things there are indeed three origins only, that which springs from an egg (oviparous), that which springs from a living being (viviparous), and that which springs from a germ.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That Being (i.e. that which had produced fire, water, and earth) thought, let me now enter those three beings (fire, water, earth) with this living Self (gîva âtmâ), and let me then reveal (develop) names and forms.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Then that Being having said, Let me make each of these three tripartite (so that fire, water, and earth should each have itself for its principal ingredient, besides an admixture of the other two) entered into those three beings (devatâ) with this living self only, and revealed names and forms.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He made each of these tripartite; and how these three beings become each of them tripartite, that learn from me now, my friend!
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'The red colour of burning fire (agni) is the colour of fire, the white colour of fire is the colour of water, the black colour of fire the colour of earth. Thus vanishes what we call fire, as a mere variety, being a name, arising from speech. What is true (satya) are the three colours (or forms).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'The red colour of the sun (âditya) is the colour of fire, the white of water, the black of earth. Thus vanishes what we call the sun, as a mere variety, being a name, arising from speech. What is true are the three colours.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'The red colour of the moon is the colour of fire, the white of water, the black of earth. Thus vanishes what we call the moon, as a mere variety, being a name, arising from speech. What is true are the three colours.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'The red colour of the lightning is the colour of fire, the white of water, the black of earth. Thus vanishes what we call the lightning, as a mere variety, being a name, arising from speech. What is true are the three colours.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Great householders and great theologians of olden times who knew this, have declared the same, saying, "No one can henceforth mention to us anything which we have not heard, perceived, or known." Out of these (three colours or forms) they knew all.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Whatever they thought looked red, they knew was the colour of fire. Whatever they thought looked white, they knew was the colour of water. Whatever they thought looked black, they knew was the colour of earth.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Whatever they thought was altogether unknown, they knew was some combination of those three beings (devatâ).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Now learn from me, my friend, how those three beings, when they reach man, become each of them tripartite.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'The earth (food) when eaten becomes threefold; its grossest portion becomes feces, its middle portion flesh, its subtilest portion mind.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Water when drunk becomes threefold; its grossest portion becomes water, its middle portion blood, its subtilest portion breath.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Fire (i.e. in oil, butter, &c.) when eaten becomes threefold; its grossest portion becomes bone, its middle portion marrow, its subtilest portion speech.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'For truly, my child, mind comes of earth, breath of water, speech of fire.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Please, Sir, inform me still more,' said the son.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Be it so, my child,' the father replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That which is the subtile portion of curds, when churned, rises upwards, and becomes butter.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'In the same manner, my child, the subtile portion of earth (food), when eaten, rises upwards, and becomes mind.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That which is the subtile portion of water, when drunk, rises upwards, and becomes breath.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That which is the subtile portion of fire, when consumed, rises upwards, and becomes speech.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'For mind, my child, comes of earth, breath of water, speech of fire.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Please, Sir, inform me still more,' said the son.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Be it so, my child,' the father replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Man (purusha), my son, consists of sixteen parts. Abstain from food for fifteen days, but drink as much water as you like, for breath comes from water, and will not be cut off, if you drink water.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Svetaketu abstained from food for fifteen days. Then he came to his father and said: 'What shall I say?' The father said: 'Repeat the Rik, Yagus, and Sâman verses.' He replied: 'They do not occur to me, Sir.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The father said to him: 'As of a great lighted fire one coal only of the size of a firefly may be left, which would not burn much more than this (i.e. very little), thus, my dear son, one part only of the sixteen parts (of you) is left, and therefore with that one part you do not remember the Vedas. Go and eat!
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Then wilt thou understand me.' Then Svetaketu ate, and afterwards approached his father. And whatever his father asked him, he knew it all by heart. Then his father said to him:
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'As of a great lighted fire one coal of the size of a firefly, if left, may be made to blaze up again by putting grass upon it, and will thus burn more than this,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Thus, my dear son, there was one part of the sixteen parts left to you, and that, lighted up with food, burnt up, and by it you remember now the Vedas.' After that, he understood what his father meant when he said: 'Mind, my son, comes from food, breath from water, speech from fire.' He understood what he said, yea, he understood it.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Uddâlaka Âruni said to his son Svetaketu: 'Learn from me the true nature of sleep (svapna). When a man sleeps here, then, my dear son, he becomes united with the True, he is gone to his own (Self). Therefore they say, svapiti, he sleeps, because he is gone (apîta) to his own (sva).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'As a bird when tied by a string flies first in every direction, and finding no rest anywhere, settles down at last on the very place where it is fastened, exactly in the same manner, my son, that mind (the gîva, or living Self in the mind, see VI, 3, 2), after flying in every direction, and finding no rest anywhere, settles down on breath; for indeed, my son, mind is fastened to breath.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Learn from me, my son, what are hunger and thirst. When a man is thus said to be hungry, water is carrying away (digests) what has been eaten by him. Therefore as they speak of a cow-leader (go-nâya), a horse-leader (asva-nâya), a man-leader (purusha-nâya), so they call water (which digests food and causes hunger) food-leader (asa-nâya). Thus (by food digested &c), my son, know this offshoot (the body) to be brought forth, for this (body) could not be without a root (cause).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And where could its root be except in food (earth)? And in the same manner, my son, as food (earth) too is an offshoot, seek after its root, viz. water. And as water too is an offshoot, seek after its root, viz. fire. And as fire too is an offshoot, seek after its root, viz. the True. Yes, all these creatures, my son, have their root in the True, they dwell in the True, they rest in the True.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'When a man is thus said to be thirsty, fire carries away what has been drunk by him. Therefore as they speak of a cow-leader (go-nâya), of a horse-leader (asva-nâya), of a man-leader (purusha-nâya), so they call fire udanyâ, thirst, i.e. water-leader. Thus (by water digested &c), my son, know this offshoot (the body) to be brought forth: this (body) could not be without a root (cause).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And where could its root be except in water? As water is an offshoot, seek after its root, viz. fire. As fire is an offshoot, seek after its root, viz. the True. Yes, all these creatures, O son, have their root in the True, they dwell in the True, they rest in the True.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And how these three beings (devatâ), fire, water, earth, O son, when they reach man, become each of them tripartite, has been said before (VI, 4, 7). When a man departs from hence, his speech is merged
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: in his mind, his mind in his breath, his breath in heat (fire), heat in the Highest Being.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Now that which is that subtile essence (the root of all), in it all that exists has its self. It is the True. It is the Self, and thou, O Svetaketu, art it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Please, Sir, inform me still more,' said the son.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Be it so, my child,' the father replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'As the bees, my son, make honey by collecting the juices of distant trees, and reduce the juice into one form,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And as these juices have no discrimination, so that they might say, I am the juice of this tree or that, in the same manner, my son, all these creatures, when they have become merged in the True (either in deep sleep or in death), know not that they are merged in the True.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Whatever these creatures are here, whether a lion, or a wolf, or a boar, or a worm, or a midge, or a gnat, or a musquito, that they become again and again.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Now that which is that subtile essence, in it all that exists has its self. It is the True. It is the Self, and thou, O Svetaketu, art it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Please, Sir, inform me still more,' said the son.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Be it so, my child,' the father replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'These rivers, my son, run, the eastern (like the Gangâ) toward the east, the western (like the Sindhu) toward the west. They go from sea to sea (i.e. the clouds lift up the water from the sea to the sky, and send it back as rain to the sea). They become indeed sea. And as those rivers, when they are in the sea, do not know, I am this or that river,
