verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'In the same manner, my son, all these creatures, when they have come back from the True, know not that they have come back from the True. Whatever these creatures are here, whether a lion, or a wolf, or a boar, or a worm, or a midge, or a gnat, or a musquito, that they become again and again.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That which is that subtile essence, in it all that exists has its self. It is the True. It is the Self, and thou, O Svetaketu, art it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Please, Sir, inform me still more,' said the son.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Be it so, my child,' the father replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: "If some one were to strike at the root of this large tree here, it would bleed, but live. If he were to strike at its stem, it would bleed, but live. If he were to strike at its top, it would bleed, but live. Pervaded by the living Self that tree stands firm, drinking in its nourishment and rejoicing;
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'But if the life (the living Self) leaves one of its branches, that branch withers; if it leaves at second, that branch withers; if it leaves a third, that branch withers. If it leaves the whole tree, the whole tree withers. In exactly the same manner, my son, know this.' Thus he spoke:
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'This (body) indeed withers and dies when the living Self has left it; the living Self dies not.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: That which is that subtile essence, in it all that exists has its self. It is the True. It is the Self, and thou, Svetaketu, art it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Please, Sir, inform me still more,' said the son.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Be it so, my child,' the father replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Fetch me from thence a fruit of the Nyagrodha tree.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Here is one, Sir.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Break it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'It is broken, Sir.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'What do you see there?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'These seeds, almost infinitesimal.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Break one of them.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'It is broken, Sir.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'What do you see there?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Not anything, Sir.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The father said: 'My son, that subtile essence which you do not perceive there, of that very essence this great Nyagrodha tree exists.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Believe it, my son. That which is the subtile essence, in it all that exists has its self. It is the True. It is the Self, and thou, O Svetaketu, art it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Please, Sir, inform me still more,' said the son.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Be it so, my child,' the father replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Place this salt in water, and then wait on me in the morning.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The son did as he was commanded.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The father said to him: 'Bring me the salt, which you placed in the water last night.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The son having looked for it, found it not, for, of course, it was melted.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The father said: 'Taste it from the surface of the water. How is it?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The son replied: 'It is salt.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Taste it from the middle. How is it?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The son replied: "It is salt.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Taste it from the bottom. How is it?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The son replied: 'It is salt.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The father said: 'Throw it away and then wait on me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He did so; but salt exists for ever.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then the father said: 'Here also, in this body, forsooth, you do not perceive the True (Sat), my son; but there indeed it is.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That which is the subtile essence, in it all that exists has its self. It is the True. It is the Self, and thou, O Svetaketu, art it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Please, Sir, inform me still more,' said the son.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Be it so, my child,' the father replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'As one might lead a person with his eyes covered away from the Gandhâras, and leave him then in a place where there are no human beings; and as that person would turn towards the east, or the north, or the west, and shout, "I have been brought here with my eyes covered, I have been left here with my eyes covered,"
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And as thereupon some one might loose his bandage and say to him, "Go in that direction, it is Gandhâra, go in that direction;" and as thereupon, having been informed and being able to judge for himself, he would by asking his way from village to village arrive at last at Gandhâra,—in exactly the same manner does a man, who meets with a teacher to inform him, obtain the true knowledge. For him there is only delay so long as he is not delivered (from the body); then he will be perfect.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That which is the subtile essence, in it all that exists has its self. It is the True. It is the Self, and thou, O Svetaketu, art it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Please, Sir, inform me still more,' said the son.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Be it so, my child,' the father replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'If a man is ill, his relatives assemble round him and ask: "Dost thou know me? Dost thou know me?" Now as long as his speech is not merged in his mind, his mind in breath, breath in heat (fire), heat in the Highest Being (devatâ), he knows them.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'But when his speech is merged in his mind, his mind in breath, breath in heat (fire), heat in the Highest Being, then he knows them not.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That which is the subtile essence, in it all that exists has its self. It is the True. It is the Self, and thou, O Svetaketu, art it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Please, Sir, inform me still more,' said the son.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Be it so, my child,' the father replied.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'My child, they bring a man hither whom they have taken by the hand, and they say: "He has taken something, he has committed a theft." (When he denies, they say), "Heat the hatchet for him." If he committed the theft, then he makes himself to be what he is not. Then the false-minded, having covered his true Self by a falsehood, grasps the heated hatchet—he is burnt, and he is killed.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'But if he did not commit the theft, then he makes himself to be what he is. Then the true-minded, having covered his true Self by truth, grasps the heated hatchet—he is not burnt, and he is delivered.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'As that (truthful) man is not burnt, thus has all that exists its self in That. It is the True. It is the Self, and thou, O Svetaketu, art it.' He understood what he said, yea, he understood it.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Nârada approached Sanatkumâra and said, 'Teach me, Sir!' Sanatkumâra said to him: 'Please to tell me what you know; afterward I shall tell you what is beyond.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Nârada said: 'I know the Rig-veda, Sir, the Yagur-veda, the Sâma-veda, as the fourth the Âtharvana, as the fifth the Itihâsa-purâna (the Bhârata); the Veda of the Vedas (grammar); the Pitrya (the rules for the sacrifices for the ancestors); the Râsi (the science of numbers); the Daiva (the science of portents); the Nidhi (the science of time); the Vâkovâkya (logic); the Ekâyana (ethics); the Devavidyâ (etymology); the Brahma-vidyâ (pronunciation, sikshâ, ceremonial, kalpa, prosody, khandas); the Bhûta-vidyâ (the science of demons); the Kshatravidyâ (the science of weapons); the Nakshatra-vidyâ (astronomy); the Sarpa and Devagana-vidyâ (the science of serpents or poisons, and the sciences of the genii, such as the making of perfumes, dancing, singing, playing, and other fine arts). All this I know, Sir.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'But, Sir, with all this I know the Mantras only, the sacred books, I do not know the Self. I have heard from men like you, that he who knows the Self overcomes grief. I am in grief. Do, Sir, help me over this grief of mine.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Sanatkumâra said to him: 'Whatever you have read, is only a name.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'A name is the Rig-veda, Yagur-veda, Sâma-veda, and as the fourth the Âtharvana, as the fifth the Itihâsa-purâna, the Veda of the Vedas, the Pitrya, the Râsi, the Daiva, the Nidhi, the Vâkovâkya, the Ekâyana, the Deva-vidyâ, the Brahma-vidyâ, the Bhûta-vidyâ, the Kshatra-vidyâ, the Nakshatra-vidyâ, the Sarpa and Devagana-vidyâ. All these are a name only. Meditate on the name.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, is there something better than a name?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Yes, there is something better than a name.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, tell it me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Speech is better than a name. Speech makes us understand the Rig-veda, Yagur-veda, Sâma-veda, and as the fourth the Âtharvana, as the fifth the Itihâsa-purâna, the Veda of the Vedas, the Pitrya, the Râsi, the Daiva, the Nidhi, the Vâkovâkya, the Ekâyana, the Deva-vidyâ, the Brahma-vidyâ, the Kshatra-vidyâ, the Nakshatra-vidyâ, the Sarpa and Devagana-vidyâ; heaven, earth, air, ether, water, fire, gods, men, cattle, birds, herbs, trees, all beasts down to worms, midges, and ants; what is right and what is wrong; what is true and what is false; what is good and what is bad; what is pleasing and what is not pleasing. For if there were no speech, neither right nor wrong would be known, neither the true nor the false, neither the good nor the bad, neither the pleasant nor the unpleasant. Speech makes us understand all this. Meditate on speech.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who meditates on speech as Brahman, is, as it were, lord and master as far as speech reaches—he who meditates on speech as Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, is there something better than speech?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Yes, there is something better than speech.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, tell it me."
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Mind (manas) is better than speech. For as the closed fist holds two amalaka or two kola or two aksha fruits, thus does mind hold speech and name. For if a man is minded in his mind to read the sacred hymns, he reads them; if he is minded in his mind to perform any actions, he performs them; if he is minded to wish for sons and cattle, he wishes for them; if he is minded to wish for this world and the other, he wishes for them. For mind is indeed the self, mind is the world, mind is Brahman. Meditate on the mind.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who meditates on the mind as Brahman, is, as it were, lord and master as far as the mind reaches—he who meditates on the mind as Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, is there something better than mind?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Yes, there is something better than mind.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, tell it me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Will (saṅkalpa) is better than mind. For when a man wills, then he thinks in his mind, then he sends forth speech, and he sends it forth in a name. In a name the sacred hymns are contained, in the sacred hymns all sacrifices.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'All these therefore (beginning with mind and ending in sacrifice) centre in will, consist of will, abide in will. Heaven and earth willed, air and ether willed, water and fire willed. Through the will of heaven and earth &c. rain wills; through the will of rain food wills; through the will of food the vital airs will; through the will of the vital airs the sacred hymns will; through the will of the sacred hymns the sacrifices will; through the will of the sacrifices the world (as their reward) wills; through the will of the world everything wills. This is will. Meditate on will.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who meditates on will as Brahman, he, being himself safe, firm, and undistressed, obtains the safe, firm, and undistressed worlds which he has willed; he is, as it were, lord and master as far as will reaches—he who meditates on will as Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, is there something better than will?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Yes, there is something better than will.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, tell it me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Consideration (kitta) is better than will. For when a man considers, then he wills, then he thinks in his mind, then he sends forth speech, and he sends it forth in a name. In a name the sacred hymns are contained, in the sacred hymns all sacrifices.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'All these (beginning with mind and ending in sacrifice) centre in consideration, consist of consideration, abide in consideration. Therefore if a man is inconsiderate, even if he possesses much learning, people say of him, he is nothing, whatever he may know; for, if he were learned, he would not be so inconsiderate. But if a man is considerate, even though he knows but little, to him indeed do people listen gladly. Consideration is the centre, consideration is the self, consideration is the support of all these. Meditate on consideration.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who meditates on consideration as Brahman, he, being himself safe, firm, and undistressed, obtains the safe, firm, and undistressed worlds which he has considered; he is, as it were, lord and master as far as consideration reaches—he who meditates on consideration as Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, is there something better than consideration?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Yes, there is something better than consideration.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, tell it me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Reflection (dhyâna) is better than consideration. The earth reflects, as it were, and thus does the sky, the heaven, the water, the mountains, gods and men. Therefore those who among men obtain greatness here on earth, seem to have obtained a part of the object of reflection (because they show a certain repose of manner). Thus while small and vulgar people are always quarrelling, abusive, and slandering, great men seem to have obtained a part of the reward of reflection. Meditate on reflection.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who meditates on reflection as Brahman, is lord and master, as it were, as far as reflection reaches—he who meditates on reflection as Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, is there something better than reflection?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Yes, there is something better than reflection.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, tell it me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Understanding (vigñâna) is better than reflection. Through understanding we understand the Rig-veda, the Yagur-veda, the Sâma-veda, and as the fourth the Âtharvana, as the fifth the tihâsapurâna, the Veda of the Vedas, the Pitrya, the Râsi, the Daiva, the Nidhi, the Vâkovâkya, the Ekâyana, the Deva-vidyâ, the Brahma-vidyâ, the Bhûta-vidyâ, the Kshatra-vidyâ, the Nakshatra-vidyâ, the Sarpa and Devagana-vidyâ, heaven, earth, air, ether, water, fire, gods, men, cattle, birds, herbs, trees, all beasts down to worms, midges, and ants; what is right and what is wrong; what is true and what is false; what is good and what is bad; what is pleasing and what is not pleasing; food and savour, this world and that, all this we understand through understanding. Meditate on understanding.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who meditates on understanding as Brahman, reaches the worlds where there is understanding and knowledge; he is, as it were, lord and master as far as understanding reaches—he who meditates on understanding as Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, is there something better than understanding?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Yes, there is something better than understanding.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, tell it me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Power (bala) is better than understanding. One powerful man shakes a hundred men of understanding. If a man is powerful, he becomes a rising man. If he rises, he becomes a man who visits wise people. If he visits, he becomes a follower of wise people. If he follows them, he becomes a seeing, a hearing, a perceiving, a knowing, a doing, an understanding man. By power the earth stands firm, and the sky, and the heaven, and the mountains, gods and men, cattle, birds, herbs, trees, all beasts down to worms, midges, and ants; by power the world stands firm. Meditate on power.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who meditates on power as Brahman, is, as it were, lord and master as far as power reaches—he who meditates on power as Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, is there something better than power?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Yes, there is something better than power.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, tell it me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Food (anna) is better than power. Therefore if a man abstain from food for ten days, though he live, he would be unable to see, hear, perceive, think, act, and understand. But when he obtains food, he is able to see, hear, perceive, think, act, and understand. Meditate on food.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who meditates on food as Brahman, obtains the worlds rich in food and drink; he is, as it were, lord and master as far as food reaches—he who meditates on food as Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, is there something better than food?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Yes, there is something better than food.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, tell it me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Water (ap) is better than food. Therefore if there is not sufficient rain, the vital spirits fail from fear that there will be less food. But if there is sufficient rain, the vital spirits rejoice, because there will be much food. This water, on assuming different forms, becomes this earth, this sky, this heaven, the mountains, gods and men, cattle, birds, herbs and trees, all beasts down to worms, midges, and ants. Water indeed assumes all these forms. Meditate on water.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who meditates on water as Brahman, obtains all wishes, he becomes satisfied; he is, as it were, lord and master as far as water reaches—he who meditates on water as Brahman.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, is there something better than water?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Yes, there is something better than water.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, tell it me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Fire (tegas) is better than water. For fire united with air, warms the ether. Then people say, It is hot, it burns, it will rain. Thus does fire, after showing this sign (itself) first, create water. And thus again thunderclaps come with lightnings, flashing upwards and across the sky. Then people say, There is lightning and thunder, it will rain. Then also does fire, after showing this sign first, create water. Meditate on fire.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who meditates on fire as Brahman, obtains, resplendent himself, resplendent worlds, full of light and free of darkness; he is, as it were, lord and master as far as fire reaches—he who meditates on fire as Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, is there something better than fire?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Yes, there is something better than fire.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, tell it me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Ether (or space) is better than fire. For in the ether exist both sun and moon, the lightning, stars, and fire (agni). Through the ether we call, through the ether we hear, through the ether we answer. In the ether or space we rejoice (when we are together), and rejoice not (when we are separated). In the ether everything is born, and towards the ether everything tends when it is born. Meditate on ether.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who meditates on ether as Brahman, obtains the worlds of ether and of light, which are free from pressure and pain, wide and spacious; he is, as it were, lord and master as far as ether reaches — he who meditates on ether as Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, is there something better than ether?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Yes, there is something better than ether.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, tell it me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Memory (smara) is better than ether. Therefore where many are assembled together, if they have no memory, they would hear no one, they would not perceive, they would not understand. Through memory we know our sons, through memory our cattle. Meditate on memory.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who meditates on memory as Brahman, is, as it were, lord and master as far as memory reaches—he who meditates on memory as Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, is there something better than memory?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Yes, there is something better than memory.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, tell it me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Hope (âsâ) is better than memory. Fired by hope does memory read the sacred hymns, perform sacrifices, desire sons and cattle, desire this world and the other. Meditate on hope.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who meditates on hope as Brahman, all his desires are fulfilled by hope, his prayers are not in vain; he is, as it were, lord and master as far as hope reaches—he who meditates on hope as Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, is there something better than hope?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Yes, there is something better than hope.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, tell it me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Spirit (prâna) is better than hope. As the spokes of a wheel hold to the nave, so does all this (beginning with names and ending in hope) hold to spirit. That spirit moves by the spirit, it gives spirit to the spirit. Father means spirit, mother is spirit, brother is spirit, sister is spirit, tutor is spirit, Brâhmana is spirit.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'For if one says anything unbecoming to a father, mother, brother, sister, tutor or Brâhmana, then people say, Shame on thee! thou hast offended thy father, mother, brother, sister, tutor, or a Brâhmana.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'But, if after the spirit has departed from them, one shoves them together with a poker, and burns them to pieces, no one would say, Thou offendest thy father, mother, brother, sister, tutor or a Brâhmana.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Spirit then is all this. He who sees this, perceives this, and understands this, becomes an ativâdin. If people say to such a man, Thou art an ativâdin, he may say, I am an ativâdin; he need not deny it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'But in reality he is an ativâdin who declares the Highest Being to be the True (Satya).'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, may I become an ativâdin by the True.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'But we must desire to know the True.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, I desire to know the True.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'When one understands the True, then one declares the True. One who does not understand it, does not declare the True. Only he who understands it, declares the True. This understanding, however, we must desire to understand.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, I desire to understand it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'When one perceives, then one understands. One who does not perceive, does not understand. Only he who perceives, understands. This perception, however, we must desire to understand.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, I desire to understand it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'When one believes, then one perceives. One who does not believe, does not perceive. Only he who believes, perceives. This belief, however, we must desire to understand.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, I desire to understand it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'When one attends on a tutor (spiritual guide), then one believes. One who does not attend on a tutor, does not believe. Only he who attends, believes. This attention on a tutor, however, we must desire to understand.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, I desire to understand it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'When one performs all sacred duties, then one attends really on a tutor. One who does not perform his duties, does not really attend on a tutor. Only he who performs his duties, attends on his tutor. This performance of duties, however, we must desire to understand.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, I desire to understand it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'When one obtains bliss (in oneself), then one performs duties. One who does not obtain bliss, does not perform duties. Only he who obtains bliss, performs duties. This bliss, however, we must desire to understand.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, I desire to understand it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'The Infinite (bhûman) is bliss. There is no bliss in anything finite. Infinity only is bliss. This Infinity, however, we must desire to understand.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, I desire to understand it.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Where one sees nothing else, hears nothing else, understands nothing else, that is the Infinite. Where one sees something else, hears something else, understands something else, that is the finite. The Infinite is immortal, the finite is mortal.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Sir, in what does the Infinite rest?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'In its own greatness—or not even in greatness.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'In the world they call cows and horses, elephants and gold, slaves, wives, fields and houses greatness. I do not mean this,' thus he spoke; 'for in that case one being (the possessor) rests in something else, (but the Infinite cannot rest in something different from itself.)
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'The Infinite indeed is below, above, behind, before, right and left—it is indeed alt this.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Now follows the explanation of the Infinite as
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: the I: I am below, I am above, I am behind, before, right and left—I am all this.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Next follows the explanation of the Infinite as the Self: Self is below, above, behind, before, right and left—Self is all this.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who sees, perceives, and understands this, loves the Self, delights in the Self, revels in the Self, rejoices in the Self—he becomes a Svarâg, (an autocrat or self-ruler); he is lord and master in all the worlds.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'But those who think differently from this, live in perishable worlds, and have other beings for their rulers.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'To him who sees, perceives, and understands this the spirit (prâna) springs from the Self, hope springs from the Self, memory springs from the Self; so do ether, fire, water, appearance and disappearance, food, power, understanding, reflection, consideration, will, mind, speech, names, sacred hymns, and sacrifices—aye, all this springs from the Self.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'There is this verse, "He who sees this, does not see death, nor illness, nor pain; he who sees this, sees everything, and obtains everything everywhere.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: '"He is one (before creation), he becomes three
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: (fire, water, earth), he becomes five, he becomes seven, he becomes nine; then again he is called the eleventh, and hundred and ten and one thousand and twenty."
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'When the intellectual aliment has been purified, the whole nature becomes purified. When the whole nature has been purified, the memory becomes firm. And when the memory (of the Highest Self) remains firm, then all the ties (which bind us to a belief in anything but the Self) are loosened.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'The venerable Sanatkumâra showed to Nârada, after his faults had been rubbed out, the other side of darkness. They call Sanatkumâra Skanda, yea, Skanda they call him.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Harih, Om. There is this city of Brahman (the body), and in it the palace, the small lotus (of the heart), and in it that small ether. Now what exists within that small ether, that is to be sought for, that is to be understood.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And if they should say to him: 'Now with regard to that city of Brahman, and the palace in it, i. e. the small lotus of the heart, and the small ether within the heart, what is there within it that deserves to be sought for, or that is to be understood?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then he should say: 'As large as this ether (all space) is, so large is that ether within the heart. Both heaven and earth are contained within it, both fire and air, both sun and moon, both lightning and stars; and whatever there is of him (the Self) here in the world, and whatever is not (i. e. whatever has been or will be), all that is contained within it.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And if they should say to him: 'If everything that exists is contained in that city of Brahman, all beings and all desires (whatever can be imagined or desired), then what is left of it, when old age reaches it and scatters it, or when it falls to pieces?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then he should say: 'By the old age of the body, that (the ether, or Brahman within it) does not age; by the death of the body, that (the ether, or Brahman within it) is not killed. That (the Brah- man) is the true Brahma-city (not the body). In it all desires are contained. It is the Self, free from sin, free from old age, from death and grief, from hunger and thirst, which desires nothing but what it ought to desire, and imagines nothing but what it ought to imagine. Now as here on earth people follow as they are commanded, and depend on the object which they are attached to, be it a country or a piece of land,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And as here on earth, whatever has been acquired by exertion, perishes, so perishes whatever is acquired for the next world by sacrifices and other good actions performed on earth. Those who depart from hence without having discovered the Self and those true desires, for them there is no freedom in all the worlds. But those who depart from hence, after having discovered the Self and those true desires, for them there is freedom in all the worlds.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Thus he who desires the world of the fathers, by his mere will the fathers come to receive him, and having obtained the world of the fathers, he is happy.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And he who desires the world of the mothers, by his mere will the mothers come to receive him, and having obtained the world of the mothers, he is happy.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And he who desires the world of the brothers, by his mere will the brothers come to receive him, and having obtained the world of the brothers, he is happy.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And he who desires the world of the sisters, by his mere will the sisters come to receive him, and having obtained the world of the sisters, he is happy.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And he who desires the world of the friends, by his mere will the friends come to receive him, and having obtained the world of the friends, he is happy.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And he who desires the world of perfumes and garlands (gandhamâlya), by his mere will perfumes and garlands come to him, and having obtained the world of perfumes and garlands, he is happy.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And he who desires the world of food and drink, by his mere will food and drink come to him, and having obtained the world of food and drink, he is happy.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And he who desires the world of song and music, by his mere will song and music come to him, and having obtained the world of song and music, he is happy.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'And he who desires the world of women, by his mere will women come to receive him, and having obtained the world of women, he is happy.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Whatever object he is attached to, whatever object he desires, by his mere will it comes to him, and having obtained it, he is happy.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'These true desires, however, are hidden by what is false; though the desires be true, they have a covering which is false. Thus, whoever belonging to us has departed this life, him we cannot gain back, so that we should see him with our eyes.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Those who belong to us, whether living or departed, and whatever else there is which we wish for and do not obtain, all that we find there (if we descend into our heart, where Brahman dwells, in the ether of the heart), There are all our true desires, but hidden by what is false. As people who do not know the country, walk again and again over a gold treasure that has been hidden somewhere in the earth and do not discover it, thus do all these creatures day after day go into the Brahma-world (they are merged in Brahman, while asleep), and yet do not discover it, because they are carried away by untruth (they do not come to themselves, i. e. they do not discover the true Self in Brahman, dwelling in the heart).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That Self abides in the heart. And this is the etymological explanation. The heart is called hridayam, instead of hrzdy-ayam, i. e. He who is in the heart. He who knows this, that He is in the heart, goes day by day (when in sushupti, deep sleep) into heaven (svarga), i.e. into the Brahman of the heart.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Now that serene being which, after having risen from out this earthly body, and having reached the highest light (self-knowledge), appears in its true form, that is the Self, thus he spoke (when asked by his pupils). This is the immortal, the fearless, this is Brahman. And of that Brahman the name is the True, Satyam,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: This name Sattyam consists of three syllables, sat-tî-yam. Sat signifies the immortal, t, the mortal, and with yam he binds both. Because he binds both, the immortal and the mortal, therefore it is yam. He who knows this goes day by day into heaven (svarga).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: That Self is a bank, a boundary, so that these worlds may not be confounded. Day and night do not pass that bank, nor old age, death, and grief; neither good nor evil deeds. All evil-doers turn back from it, for the world of Brahman is free from all evil.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Therefore he who has crossed that bank, if blind, ceases to be blind; if wounded, ceases to be wounded; if afflicted, ceases to be afflicted. Therefore when that bank has been crossed, night becomes day indeed, for the world of Brahman is lighted up once for all.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: What people call sacrifice (yagña), that is really abstinence (brahmakarya). For he who knows, obtains that (world of Brahman, which others obtain by sacrifice), by means of abstinence.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: What people call sacrifice (ishta), that is really abstinence, for by abstinence, having searched (ishtvâ), he obtains the Self.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: What people call sacrifice (sattrâyana), that is really abstinence, for by abstinence he obtains from the Sat (the true), the safety (trâna) of the Self.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: What people call the vow of silence (mauna), that is really abstinence, for he who by abstinence has found out the Self, meditates (manute).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: What people call fasting (aranyâyana), that is really abstinence, for that Self does not perish (na nasyati), which we find out by abstinence.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: What people call a hermit's life (aranyâyana), that is really abstinence. Ara and Nya are two lakes in the world of Brahman, in the third heaven from hence; and there is the lake Airammadîya, and the Asvattha tree, showering down Soma, and the city of Brahman (Hiranyagarbha) Aparâgitâ, and the golden Prabhuvimita (the hall built by Prabhu, Brahman).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Now that world of Brahman belongs to those who find the lakes Ara and Nya in the world of Brahman by means of abstinence; for them there is freedom in all the worlds.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Now those arteries of the heart consist of a brown substance, of a white, blue, yellow, and red substance, and so is the sun brown, white, blue, yellow, and red.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: As a very long highway goes to two places, to one at the beginning, and to another at the end, so do the rays of the sun go to both worlds, to this one and to the other. They start from the sun, and enter into those arteries; they start from those arteries, and enter into the sun.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And when a man is asleep, reposing, and at perfect rest, so that he sees no dream, then he has entered into those arteries. Then no evil touches him, for he has obtained the light (of the sun).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And when a man falls ill, then those who sit round him, say, 'Do you know me? Do you know me?' As long as he has not departed from this body, he knows them.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: But when he departs from this body, then he departs upwards by those very rays (towards the worlds which he has gained by merit, not by knowledge); or he goes out while meditating on Om (and thus securing an entrance into the Brahma- loka). And while his mind is failing, he is going to the sun. For the sun is the door of the world (of Brahman). Those who know, walk in; those who do not know, are shut out. There is this verse: 'There are a hundred and one arteries of the heart; one of them penetrates the crown of the head; moving upwards by it a man reaches the immortal; the others serve for departing in different directions, yea, in different directions.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Pragâpati said: 'The Self which is free from sin, free from old age, from death and grief, from hunger and thirst, which desires nothing but what it ought to desire, and imagines nothing but what it ought to imagine, that it is which we must search out, that it is which we must try to understand. He who has searched out that Self and understands it, obtains all worlds and all desires.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The Devas (gods) and Asuras (demons) both heard these words, and said: 'Well, let us search for that Self by which, if one has searched it out, all worlds and all desires are obtained.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Thus saying Indra went from the Devas, Virokana from the Asuras, and both, without having communicated with each other, approached Pragâpati,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: holding fuel in their hands, as is the custom for pupils approaching their master.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They dwelt there as pupils for thirty-two years. Then Pragâpati asked them: 'For what purpose have you both dwelt here?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They replied: 'A saying of yours is being repeated, viz. "the Self which is free from sin, free from old age, from death and grief, from hunger and thirst, which desires nothing but what it ought to desire, and imagines nothing but what it ought to imagine, that it is which we must search out, that it is which we must try to understand. He who has searched out that Self and understands it, obtains all worlds and all desires." Now we both have dwelt here because we wish for that Self.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Pragâpati said to them: 'The person that is seen in the eye, that is the Self. This is what I have said. This is the immortal, the fearless, this is Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They asked: 'Sir, he who is perceived in the water, and he who is perceived in a mirror, who is he?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He replied: 'He himself indeed is seen in all these.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Look at your Self in a pan of water, and whatever you do not understand of your Self, come and tell me.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They looked in the water-pan. Then Pragâpati said to them: 'What do you see?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They said: 'We both see the self thus altogether, a picture even to the very hairs and nails.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Pragâpati said to them: 'After you have adorned yourselves, have put on your best clothes and cleaned yourselves, look again into the water-pan.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They, after having adorned themselves, having put on their best clothes and cleaned themselves, looked into the water-pan.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Pragâpati said: 'What do you see?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They said: 'Just as we are, well adorned, with our best clothes and clean, thus we are both there, Sir, well adorned, with our best clothes and clean.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Pragâpati said: 'That is the Self, this is the immortal, the fearless, this is Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then both went away satisfied in their hearts.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And Pragâpati, looking after them, said: 'They both go away without having perceived and without having known the Self, and whoever of these two, whether Devas or Asuras, will follow this doctrine (upanishad), will perish.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Now Virokhana, satisfied in his heart, went to the Asuras and preached that doctrine to them, that the self (the body) alone is to be worshipped, that the
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: self (the body) alone is to be served, and that he who worships the self and serves the self, gains both worlds, this and the next.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Therefore they call even now a man who does not give alms here, who has no faith, and offers no sacrifices, an Âsura, for this is the doctrine (upanishad) of the Asuras. They deck out the body of the dead with perfumes, flowers, and fine raiment by way of ornament, and think they will thus conquer that world.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: But Indra, before he had returned to the Devas, saw this difficulty. As this self (the shadow in the water) is well adorned, when the body is well adorned, well dressed, when the body is well dressed, well cleaned, if the body is well cleaned, that self will also be blind, if the body is blind, lame, if the body is lame, crippled, if the body is crippled, and will perish in fact as soon as the body perishes. Therefore I see no good in this (doctrine).
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Taking fuel in his hand he came again as a pupil to Pragâpati. Pragâpati said to him: 'Maghavat (Indra), as you went away with Virokana, satisfied in your heart, for what purpose did you come back?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said: 'Sir, as this self (the shadow) is well adorned, when the body is well adorned, well dressed, when the body is well dressed, well cleaned, if the body is well cleaned, that self will also be blind, if the body is blind, lame, if the body is lame, crippled, if the body is crippled, and will perish in fact as soon as the body perishes. Therefore I see no good in this (doctrine).'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'So it is indeed, Maghavat,' replied Pragâpati; 'but I shall explain him (the true Self) further to you. Live with me another thirty-two years.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He lived with him another thirty-two years, and then Pragâpati said:
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who moves about happy in dreams, he is the Self, this is the immortal, the fearless, this is Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then Indra went away satisfied in his heart. But before he had returned to the Devas, he saw this difficulty. Although it is true that that self is not blind, even if the body is blind, nor lame, if the body is lame, though it is true that that self is not rendered faulty by the faults of it (the body),
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Nor struck when it (the body) is struck, nor lamed when it is lamed, yet it is as if they struck him (the self) in dreams, as if they chased him. He becomes even conscious, as it were, of pain, and sheds tears. Therefore I see no good in this.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Taking fuel in his hands, he went again as a pupil to Pragâpati. Pragâpati said to him: 'Maghavat, as you went away satisfied in your heart, for what purpose did you come back?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said: 'Sir, although it is true that that self is not blind even if the body is blind, nor lame, if the body is lame, though it is true that that self is not rendered faulty by the faults of it (the body),
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Nor struck when it (the body) is struck, nor lamed when it is lamed, yet it is as if they struck him (the self) in dreams, as if they chased him. He becomes even conscious, as it were, of pain, and sheds tears. Therefore I see no good in this.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'So it is indeed, Maghavat,' replied Pragâpati; 'but I shall explain him (the true Self) further to you. Live with me another thirty-two years.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He lived with him another thirty-two years. Then Pragâpati said:
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'When a man being asleep, reposing, and at perfect rest sees no dreams, that is the Self, this is the immortal, the fearless, this is Brahman.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then Indra went away satisfied in his heart. But before he had returned to the Devas, he saw this difficulty. In truth he thus does not know himself (his self) that he is I, nor does he know anything that exists. He is gone to utter annihilation. I see no good in this.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Taking fuel in his hand he went again as a pupil to Pragâpati. Pragâpati said to him: 'Maghavat, as you went away satisfied in your heart, for what purpose did you come back?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He said: 'Sir, in that way he does not know himself (his self) that he is I, nor does he know anything that exists. He is gone to utter annihilation. I see no good in this.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'So it is indeed, Maghavat,' replied Pragâpati; 'but I shall explain him (the true Self) further to you, and nothing more than this. Live here other five years.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He lived there other five years. This made in all one hundred and one years, and therefore it is said that Indra Maghavat lived one hundred and one years as a pupil with Pragâpati. Pragâpati said to him:
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Maghavat, this body is mortal and always held by death. It is the abode of that Self which is immortal and without body. When in the body (by thinking this body is I and I am this body) the Self is held by pleasure and pain. So long as he is in the body, he cannot get free from pleasure and pain. But when he is free of the body (when he knows himself different from the body), then neither pleasure nor pain touches him.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'The wind is without body, the cloud, lightning, and thunder are without body (without hands, feet, &c.) Now as these, arising from this heavenly ether (space), appear in their own form, as soon as they have approached the highest light,
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Thus does that serene being, arising from this body, appear in its own form, as soon as it has approached the highest light (the knowledge of Self). He (in that state) is the highest person (uttama pfirusha). He moves about there laughing (or eating), playing, and rejoicing (in his mind), be it with women, carriages, or relatives, never minding that body into which he was born.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Like as a horse attached to a cart, so is the spirit (prâna, pragñâtman) attached to this body.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'Now where the sight has entered into the void (the open space, the black pupil of the eye), there is the person of the eye, the eye itself is the instrument of seeing. He who knows, let me smell this, he is the Self, the nose is the instrument of smelling. He who knows, let me say this, he is the Self, the tongue is the instrument of saying. He who knows, let me hear this, he is the Self, the ear is the instrument of hearing.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who knows, let me think this, he is the Self, the mind is his divine eye. He, the Self, seeing these pleasures (which to others are hidden like a buried treasure of gold) through his divine eye, i. e. the mind, rejoices.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'The Devas who are in the world of Brahman meditate on that Self (as taught by Pragâpati to Indra, and by Indra to the Devas). Therefore all worlds belong to them, and all desires. He who knows that Self and understands it, obtains all worlds and all desires.' Thus said Pragâpati, yea, thus said Pragâpati.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: From the dark (the Brahman of the heart) I come to the nebulous (the world of Brahman), from the nebulous to the dark, shaking off all evil, as a horse shakes his hairs, and as the moon frees herself from the mouth of Râhu. Having shaken off the body, I obtain, self made and satisfied, the uncreated world of Brahman, yea, I obtain it.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He who is called ether (âkâsa) is the revealer of all forms and names. That within which these forms and names are contained is the Brahman, the Immortal, the Self.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: I come to the hall of Pragâpati, to the house; I am the glorious among Brâhmans, glorious among princes, glorious among men. I obtained that glory, I am glorious among the glorious. May I never go to the white, toothless, yet devouring, white abode; may I never go to it.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Brahmâ (Hiranyagarbha or Paramesvara) told this to Pragâpati (Kasyapa), Pra'gâpati to Manu (his son), Manu to mankind. He who has learnt the Veda from a family of teachers, according to the sacred rule, in the leisure time left from the duties to be performed for the Guru, who, after receiving his discharge, has settled in his own house, keeping up the memory of what he has learnt by repeating it regularly in some sacred spot, who has begotten virtuous sons, and concentrated all his senses on the Self, never giving pain to any creature, except at the tîrthas (sacrifices, &c), he who behaves thus all his life, reaches the world of Brahman, and does not return, yea, he does not return.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The Pupil asks: 'At whose wish does the mind sent forth proceed on its errand? At whose command does the first breath go forth? At whose wish do we utter this speech? What god directs the eye, or the ear?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The Teacher replies: It is the ear of the ear, the mind of the mind, the speech of speech, the breath of breath, and the eye of the eye. When freed (from the senses) the wise, on departing from this world, become immortal.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'The eye does not go thither, nor speech, nor mind. We do not know, we do not understand, how any one can teach it.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'It is different from the known, it is also above the unknown, thus we have heard from those of old, who taught us this.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That which is not expressed by speech and by which speech is expressed, that alone know as Brahman, not that which people here adore.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That which does not think by mind, and by which, they say, mind is thought, that alone know as Brahman, not that which people here adore.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That which does not see by the eye, and by which one sees (the work of) the eyes, that alone know as Brahman, not that which people here adore.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That which does not hear by the ear, and by which the ear is heard, that alone know as Brahman, not that which people here adore.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'That which does not breathe by breath, and by which breath is drawn, that alone know as Brahman, not that which people here adore.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The Teacher says: 'If thou thinkest I know it well; then thou knowest surely but little, what is that form of Brahman known, it may be, to thee?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The Pupil says: 'I do not think I know it well, nor do I know that I do not know it. He among us who knows this, he knows it, nor does he know that he does not know it.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He by whom it (Brahman) is not thought, by him it is thought; he by whom it is thought, knows it not. It is not understood by those who understand it, it is understood by those who do not understand it.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'It is thought to be known (as if) by awakening, and (then) we obtain immortality indeed. By the Self we obtain strength, by knowledge we obtain immortality.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'If a man know this here, that is the true (end of life); if he does not know this here, then there is great destruction (new births). The wise who have thought on all things (and recognised the Self in them) become immortal, when they have departed from this world.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Brahman obtained the victory for the Devas. The Devas became elated by the victory of Brahman, and they thought, this victory is ours only, this greatness is ours only.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Brahman perceived this and appeared to them. But they did not know it, and said: 'What sprite (yaksha or yakshya) is this?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: They said to Agni (fire): 'O Gâtavedas, find out what sprite this is.' 'Yes,' he said.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He ran toward it, and Brahman said to him: 'Who are you?' He replied: 'I am Agni, I am Gâtavedas.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Brahman said: 'What power is in you?' Agni replied: 'I could burn all whatever there is on earth.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Brahman put a straw before him, saying: 'Burn this.' He went towards it with all his might, but he could not burn it. Then he returned thence and said: 'I could not find out what sprite this is.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then they said to Vâyu (air): 'O Vâyu, find out what sprite this is.' 'Yes,' he said.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He ran toward it, and Brahman said to him: 'Who are you?' He replied: 'I am Vâyu, I am Mâtarisvan.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Brahman said: 'What power is in you?' Vâyu replied: 'I could take up all whatever there is on earth.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Brahman put a straw before him, saying: 'Take it up.' He went towards it with all his might, but he could not take it up. Then he returned thence and said: 'I could not find out what sprite this is.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then they said to Indra: 'O Maghavan, find out what sprite this is.' He went towards it, but it disappeared from before him.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Then in the same space (ether) he came towards a woman, highly adorned: it was Umâ, the daughter of Himavat. He said to her: 'Who is that sprite?'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: She replied: 'It is Brahman. It is through the victory of Brahman that you have thus become great.' After that he knew that it was Brahman.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Therefore these Devas, viz. Agni, Vâyu, and Indra, are, as it were, above the other gods, for they touched it (the Brahman) nearest.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And therefore Indra is, as it were, above the other gods, for he touched it nearest, he first knew it.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: This is the teaching of Brahman, with regard to the gods (mythological): It is that which now flashes forth in the lightning, and now vanishes again.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: And this is the teaching of Brahman, with regard to the body (psychological): It is that which seems to move as mind, and by it imagination remembers again and again.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: That Brahman is called Tadvana, by the name of Tadvana it is to be meditated on. All beings have a desire for him who knows this.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The Teacher: 'As you have asked me to tell you the Upanishad, the Upanishad has now been told you. We have told you the Brâhmî Upanishad.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'The feet on which that Upanishad stands are penance, restraint, sacrifice; the Vedas are all its limbs, the True is its abode.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: 'He who knows this Upanishad, and has shaken off all evil, stands in the endless, unconquerable world of heaven, yea, in the world of heaven.'
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Vâgasravasa, desirous (of heavenly rewards), surrendered (at a sacrifice) all that he possessed. He had a son of the name of Nakiketas.
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: When the (promised) presents were being given (to the priests), faith entered into the heart of Nakiketas, who was still a boy, and he thought:
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: "Unblessed, surely, are the worlds to which a man goes by giving (as his promised present at a sacrifice) cows which have drunk water, eaten hay, given their milk, and are barren."
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: He (knowing that his father had promised to give up all that he possessed, and therefore his son also) said to his father: "Dear father, to whom wilt thou give me?" He said it a second and a third time. Then the father replied (angrily): "I shall give thee unto Death." (The father, having once said so, though in haste, had to be true to his word and to sacrifice his son.)
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: The son said: "I go as the first, at the head of many (who have still to die); I go in the midst of many (who are now dying). What will be the work of Yama (the ruler of the departed) which to-day he has to do unto me?
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)

verses.translation: Look back how it was with those who came before, look forward how it will be with those who come hereafter. A mortal ripens like corn, like corn he springs up again." (Nakiketas enters into the abode of Yama Vaivasvata, and there is no one to receive him. Thereupon one of the attendants of Yama is supposed to say:)
verses.translationName: The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East, vols. I and XV)
